Title: Vestland's RM2bil order book to drive earnings growth: Kenanga Research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd is expected to post earnings of RM49.4 million and RM77.5 million in the financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY27, respectively, backed by its outstanding order book and tender book.
Kenanga Research said the company has an order book of RM2 billion and a tender book of RM5 billion.
It valued Vestland at a price-to-earnings ratio target of 16 times its FY27 earnings to derive a fair value of RM1.20.
"Despite its smaller market capitalisation, we assign a mid-cap construction valuation multiple of 16 times to reflect its strong near-term earnings growth profile," it said in a note.
Kenanga Research noted that Vestland sets itself apart in the construction sector by leveraging a specialised design-and-build model, positioning itself as an end-to-end solutions provider rather than a conventional contractor.
Additionally, the firm said Vestland's net margin bottomed out at 4.5 per cent in FY25, down from eight per cent in FY23, due to higher material and fuel costs, alongside a project mix shift toward larger contracts with tighter margins.
However, profit margins are expected to rebound moving forward, driven by accelerated cash collection cycles from public infrastructure contracts, a superior margin mix for public sector work versus private projects and a rising share of public sector jobs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Give young candidates a chance to prove their worth, says Adam Adli
Article:
MELAKA: Young people should not be deemed too inexperienced to contest elections when political parties have long relied on them to carry out much of their campaign work, acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said
He said it was unfair to question the suitability of young candidates based solely on their age when they were often the backbone of election campaigns.
"Look at any political party. It is the young people who put up flags, hang banners, gather crowds for speeches, distribute flyers and even argue on social media.
"But when it comes to becoming candidates, suddenly they are considered too young. That makes things difficult," he said at a Pakatan Harapan daily press conference here today.
Adam Adli, who is also deputy higher education minister, was responding to questions on whether PH's younger candidates could convince older voters who remained sceptical about their experience and capabilities.
PH has fielded several young candidates for the Melaka election, including Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, 24, in Kuala Linggi, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, 26, in Klebang, and Jason Tze-Xi Nathan, 31, in Pengkalan Batu.
Adam Adli said the coalition's decision to field younger candidates was aimed at ensuring that elected representatives reflected the electorate's demographics, particularly following the implementation of Undi18 and automatic voter registration.
He said young candidates should not be judged solely on their political experience or communication skills, which might differ from those of more seasoned politicians.
"We must acknowledge that there is still an old stigma surrounding young candidates. Many face pressure because they supposedly lack experience or do not communicate in the same way as older politicians.
"But if we do not start giving them opportunities now, how can they gain the experience needed in the next five or 10 years?
"We hope they can begin gaining that experience now," he said.
However, he acknowledged that fielding young candidates did not necessarily guarantee support from younger voters.
"We cannot assume that just because we have young candidates, we will automatically win young voters. The mathematics does not work that way," he said.
He said young voters' political preferences were shaped by various factors, including their families, parents, social surroundings and political beliefs.
As such, younger candidates must demonstrate their ability to appeal not only to their peers but also to older generations.
Adam Adli added that PH had also introduced the "Trak Pilih Harapan" initiative as part of its campaign strategy to engage younger voters through a more relaxed and interactive approach.
He said although the truck was equipped to host political speeches, the coalition had opted to use it as a space for informal discussions over coffee, allowing young people to interact directly with candidates and party leaders rather than simply listening to conventional campaign speeches.
Meanwhile, Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition's candidates, regardless of age, would ultimately be judged by their ability to understand and address issues affecting their constituencies.
He said younger candidates in constituencies such as Kuala Linggi, Klebang and Pengkalan Batu had been actively engaging with residents to understand their concerns.
"Whether they are young, middle-aged or older, our focus is on how they understand the issues affecting their respective constituencies and find solutions.
"Although their experience may differ, their objective remains the same, which is to help the people resolve the problems they face," he said.
Adly said younger candidates could also serve as a bridge between the coalition and younger voters, particularly in identifying economic opportunities and issues affecting their future.
However, he agreed that youth voting patterns were influenced by several factors beyond candidates' ages, including family members, peers and social media.
He said PH would take these factors into account in its efforts to secure support from younger voters in the election.

Title: Good service doesn't exempt public officers from the law, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public officers who demonstrate good performance and contribute to the country deserve recognition but are not exempt from the rule of law, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said no one should be exempt from legal obligations, regardless of their service record or contributions, and that the rule of law must always be respected and upheld.
Responding to questions about the action taken against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, Anwar said the matter stemmed from a police report and must be investigated in accordance with established procedures.
"We must remember that an officer's distinguished service record or outstanding performance does not exempt them from complying with the law and regulations.
"If there are allegations or accusations that an individual has been assaulted or has engaged in misconduct, the matter must be dealt with through the appropriate legal process," he said.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) during the Minister's Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar pointed out that even senior police officers, including former inspectors-general of police, had faced legal action and imprisonment for offences.
"Does that mean they have never rendered any service? Of course not. They have made their own contributions and rendered valuable service," he said.
Anwar stressed that two principles must be distinguished: public officers must perform their duties professionally and demonstrate good performance, while any alleged breach of the law must be addressed through the appropriate investigative and legal processes.

Title: Immigration steps up 3 operations to curb employment of undocumented migrants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is carrying out three targeted operations to curb the presence of undocumented migrants in the employment sector and prevent their involvement in unauthorised business activities.
The operations, known as Op Hijau, Op Jaja and Op Belanja, are being conducted by the Home Ministry and the Immigration Department.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government continued to conduct enforcement operations to address the presence of foreigners, particularly undocumented migrants.
"Among the approaches adopted are targeted enforcement operations, such as Op Hijau, which focuses on the agricultural sector, including crop plantations, livestock farms and nurseries.
"Op Jaja targets hawking activities at night markets, farmers' markets, wholesale markets, fruit stalls and roadside stalls, while Op Belanja focuses on supermarkets, grocery shops, furniture shops and other identified business premises," he said in a written reply published on the parliament website last night.
He was responding to a question from Dr Abd Ghani Ahmad (PN-Jerlun) on the government's measures to curb the growing presence of foreigners, including undocumented migrants, working in agriculture, plantations and grocery shops.
Saifuddin said the Immigration Department had conducted 2,644 operations under the three targeted initiatives between Jan 1, 2025, and Sept 15 this year.
"A total of 19,192 people were inspected during the operations, resulting in the arrest of 4,168 undocumented migrants and 299 employers suspected of committing immigration-related offences.
"Besides targeted operations, the Immigration Department has strengthened enforcement inspections to improve monitoring, checks and compliance at locations identified as high-risk areas for pass abuse, the employment of undocumented migrants or the involvement of foreigners in unauthorised work.
"During the same period, the department conducted 11,790 enforcement inspections nationwide," he said.
He said enforcement was also carried out through joint operations involving local authorities, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Companies Commission of Malaysia.
"This approach enables more comprehensive action to be taken within the respective agencies' jurisdictions, covering immigration status, business licences and compliance with relevant regulations.
"During the same period, 685 joint operations were conducted," he said.
Saifuddin added that the Immigration Department had also deployed officers under an omnipresence approach to increase the visibility and presence of enforcement personnel.
"This approach serves as a deterrent against the employment of undocumented migrants and the involvement of foreigners in illegal economic activities.
"The Home Ministry, through the Immigration Department, will continue to intensify intelligence-led operations and act on public complaints, while strengthening inter-agency cooperation to ensure enforcement is comprehensive, consistent and effective," he said.

Title: Rafizi at Bukit Aman over RM9.5mil bribery allegation against Ramanan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli arrived at Bukit Aman today to have his statement recorded over allegations that PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan received a RM9.5 million bribe in connection with the corporate mafia issue.

Title: Tanjung Bungah residents demand halt to Sore Thumb development
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Tanjung Bungah residents staged a demonstration outside the state legislative assembly building today, demanding that the government immediately halt a developer's plans to alter the natural Sore Thumb promontory.
They accused
the authorities of breaking longstanding promises
by allowing public coastal land to be used for a private five-storey wellness centre.
The protest comes in the wake of the deadly landslide in Paya Terubong on Oct 25. Residents warned that extensive engineering works on natural terrain could invite disaster.
Tanjung Bungah Residents' Association (TBRA) chairman Zulfikar Aziz criticised the developer's plans to reduce the lush hill from 18m to six metres, remove mature vegetation and build a massive concrete seawall along the public shoreline.
"We want a public park, but not at the expense of the very natural environment it should protect," he said, criticising plans to build concrete jogging tracks over fragile coastal habitats.
"A coastal park should coexist with nature, not destroy it," he added.
Resident Oo Huei Ying warned that extending a hard retaining wall beyond the actual high-water mark could disturb seabed sand and trigger severe erosion along the Tanjung Bungah and Batu Ferringhi coastlines.
"This is not a public park; it is an engineered extension of a private commercial project," she said.
She questioned why residents had to continue negotiating with private interests while their own 78-page architect-designed master plan, submitted in February, had yet to be considered.
The promontory, which was formed following illegal dumping two decades ago, has since regenerated into a habitat for otters, white-faced dusky leaf monkeys and nesting sea eagles.
Residents also pointed out that Penang was already falling short of the mandatory open-space ratios set out in its draft Structure Plan 2040 (RSN 2040).
They said the loss of natural green space would therefore be difficult to justify.
Calling on Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow to honour his pledges to protect the promontory's natural character, the residents offered to raise funds through crowdfunding to develop the park themselves and prevent the area from being covered in concrete.
A timeline provided by the residents showed that planning permission for Lot 4658 had not been secured at a meeting on Feb 17, 2022, with then state executive councillor Zairil Khir Johari.
At the meeting, the developer was instructed to build a public park.
On March 28 that year, Chow chaired a meeting at which he stipulated that a two-acre seaside public park must be established before any commercial development could proceed.
Chow also directed that Sore Thumb be gazetted as a green lung. The area was officially gazetted as open space on Nov 27, 2023.
However, residents alleged that planning permission for Lot 4658 was granted in March 2025 without affected neighbours receiving individual notices or being given an opportunity to raise objections.
Alarmed by site-clearing works encroaching on the promontory and beach, residents wrote to Chow on Oct 24, 2025, demanding an immediate halt to the work.
During a follow-up meeting with the chief minister on Nov 6, 2025, community members called for the ecosystem to remain untouched.
They said they secured pledges to suspend tree-felling, consult residents on landscape plans and safeguard the coastline.
Following tripartite discussions in mid-January this year, residents submitted their 78-page architect-designed master plan on Feb 10.
Endorsed by civil society and environmental groups, the proposal calls on the state to preserve the wildlife habitat and natural terrain.
It proposes low-impact nature trails and scenic lookouts instead of extensive concrete infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Binance reaffirms commitment to Malaysia return, absorbs US$6.3bil impact
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Binance has reiterated its commitment to engaging with Malaysian regulators over a potential licensed return to the country and absorbing the financial impact of a recent US$6.3 billion (RM25.6 billion) security breach.
The response comes after the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange confirmed it had been in discussions with the Securities Commission (SC) and Bank Negara Malaysia over the past 10 months on a licensed pathway back into the local market.
This comes more than five years after the SC ordered Binance to cease operations in Malaysia in 2021.
Responding to Business Times' queries, a Binance spokesperson said the company remained committed to working constructively with both regulators.
"We remain committed to engaging constructively with the Securities Commission Malaysia and Bank Negara Malaysia as we work towards bringing long-term value to Malaysians in a fully compliant manner.
"We are not able to disclose further details on our discussions at this stage," they added.
On the recent security incident, Binance said it had covered 95 per cent of the affected assets and would bear the full financial impact of the stolen funds, rather than passing the losses on to users.
The company said it was in the process of purchasing the remaining five per cent, which comprised less-liquid assets, and would provide further updates as the process was finalised.
It added that precautionary measures had been implemented to safeguard the platform, alongside security assessments and service readiness checks following the breach.
Binance said withdrawals were being restored progressively as those checks were completed, while deposit services had remained open throughout.
"User funds remain safe. Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users," the spokesperson said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI firm Anthropic posts US$104bil losses ahead of IPO
Article:
SAN JOSE: The AI company Anthropic has accumulated losses of US$104 billion since the start of the year, according to its updated prospectus filed on Monday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
Meanwhile, its revenue soared to US$33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from US$2.5 billion in the same period last year.
In the first three quarters of 2025, losses totalled US$25 billion.
Anthropic is expected to go public in the coming weeks, overtaking ChatGPT developer OpenAI, which no longer plans to list its shares this year.
In the updated prospectus, Anthropic included its financial results for the third quarter, reporting a loss of US$23.3 billion on revenue of US$17 billion.
The losses were largely attributable to an accounting adjustment, while the operating loss stood at US$567 million.
Artificial intelligence developers are currently investing heavily in developing their AI models and expanding their computing capacity.
In the last quarter, Anthropic spent around US$5 billion on computing resources.
The updated prospectus also revealed that the company had already budgeted US$895 billion for data centre capacity and infrastructure expansion over the coming years.
Of this amount, just under US$450 billion is due before the end of 2030.
Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, competes not only with ChatGPT but also with technology heavyweights such as Google, Microsoft and Meta.
Investors' long-standing concerns about whether massive investments in AI can generate sufficient returns have recently resurfaced.
There is also growing debate about the risks posed by the technology following independent hacking attacks carried out using AI software.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dialog's RM200mil tank expansion to bolster recurring income
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts view Dialog Group Bhd's latest expansion of its petroleum product storage capacity in Tanjung Langsat, Johor, positively, saying it will strengthen the group's recurring income base and support its midstream growth prospects.
Earnings contributions from the expansion are expected from the financial year ending June 2030 (FY30).
Dialog announced an additional 100,000 cubic metres (cbm) storage capacity at its wholly owned Dialog Terminals Langsat 3 (DTL3), with completion targeted by mid-2029.
The expansion, estimated to cost up to RM200 million, will increase DTL3's capacity by 26 per cent to 480,000 cbm from 380,000 cbm currently, bringing Dialog's total storage capacity at Tanjung Langsat to more than 1.1 million cbm.
Public Investment Bank Bhd said the development would broaden Dialog's recurring income base while making use of its existing marine facilities.
It said management was targeting a high single-digit internal rate of return (IRR) for the project, consistent with its previous terminal developments.
The firm noted that the latest expansion would operate under an independent storage model, with leasing tenures expected to range from six to 12 months and rates benchmarked against S&P Global Platts market indications.
This would allow leasing rates to be adjusted according to prevailing market conditions, although earnings would depend on utilisation and pricing when the additional capacity is commissioned.
The commercial structure differs from the previous 150,000 cbm expansion, which began operations in September 2026 and is fully contracted, including 100,000 cbm dedicated to EcoCeres under a take-or-pay arrangement.
Public Investment Bank expects the latest capacity to achieve utilisation of more than 90 per cent following commissioning, supported by regional storage demand and potential demand for greater supply and logistics flexibility amid geopolitical uncertainties.
The project translates into an estimated capital expenditure of up to RM2,000 per cbm, with Dialog's engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) division undertaking the construction works, which are expected to begin immediately.
However, Public Investment Bank noted that the Tanjung Langsat terminal site was almost fully developed, suggesting limited room for further capacity additions after the latest expansion.
It maintained its earnings forecasts, with contributions from the project expected mainly from FY30 onwards, while keeping its "Neutral" recommendation on Dialog and target price of RM2.10 unchanged.
Separately, RHB Research said the expansion reinforced Dialog's strategy of growing its recurring midstream income, with the group's storage operations continuing to provide stable earnings visibility.
It noted that utilisation rates across Dialog's tank terminal assets remained above 90 per cent, while independent storage rates were stable at between S$6 and S$6.50 per cbm per month.
The firm said the group's midstream growth prospects were also supported by Phase Three of the Pengerang Deepwater Terminals expansion, which will add 614,000 cbm of storage capacity, with BP Singapore as its dedicated long-term customer.
The project could generate annual terminal revenue of between RM135 million and RM150 million upon full commissioning, it said.
RHB Research maintained its FY27 to FY29 earnings forecasts, as meaningful contributions from the latest DTL3 expansion were expected only from FY30 onwards.
It retained its "Buy" recommendation and RM2.44 target price, based on a sum-of-parts valuation covering Dialog's core business, terminal assets and upstream operations, with a six per cent environmental, social and governance discount.
The firm identified lower oil prices, weaker tank storage rates and lower utilisation of independent storage terminals as key downside risks.

Title: STR, Sara effectiveness should be measured by overall benefits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The effectiveness of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) should not be measured solely by the amount of assistance received, but by how effectively the two schemes work together to ease the financial burden on households.
Economist Professor Emeritus Dr Barjoyai Bardai of the Malaysia University of Science and Technology (MUST) said the increase in the combined allocation for STR and SARA to RM16 billion next year should be assessed based on the overall benefits to recipients, including how well the assistance meets their basic needs and improves their purchasing power.
He said this approach would provide a clearer picture of how effective the government's efforts were in helping Malaysians cope with rising living costs.
"The success of STR and SARA in 2027 should not be judged simply by whether cash assistance has increased or decreased.
"We need to look at the total assistance received, whether it reaches the intended groups and how effectively it improves purchasing power and eases cost-of-living pressures," he told Bernama.
Barjoyai said the combination of cash assistance and targeted support for basic necessities allowed recipients to meet different household needs, with STR providing the flexibility to pay utility bills, transport costs and children's education expenses, while SARA helped cover the cost of essential goods.
"By providing credit specifically for essential purchases, the scheme helps reduce households' daily expenses," he said.
He said determining whether the assistance was sufficient required consideration of the total amount received annually under STR and SARA, the number of dependants, household income, place of residence and spending patterns.
Barjoyai also welcomed the expansion of SARA to cover fresh produce and other perishable goods at farmers' markets and tamu under the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA), saying it would give recipients greater choice in meeting their families' nutritional needs.
"Previously, the assistance was largely limited to selected grocery items. With this expansion, recipients will have more options to meet their families' nutritional needs," he said.
He said extending SARA Madani aid to Malaysians aged 18 and above who were not STR recipients would also broaden the social safety net to include those affected by rising living costs.
[[nid:1569604]]
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Faculty of Business and Management's Department of Economics and Financial Studies senior lecturer Dr Mohd Rahim Khamis said STR and SARA complemented each other in helping households afford basic necessities and cushion the impact of rising prices on daily expenses.
"Both schemes can help protect household spending on basic necessities from rising prices.
"Their effectiveness ultimately depends on whether recipients can continue to afford sufficient essential goods despite the increasing cost of living," he said.
He said expanding SARA could also stimulate economic activity in the agricultural and agro-based sectors, help small and medium-sized traders earn more income and support the long-term viability of participating businesses.
Mohd Rahim said extending SARA MADANI to those who did not qualify for STR was a positive move, as rising living costs also affected households beyond the low-income group.
He added that household finances should be assessed based on disposable income after taking into account financial commitments and daily expenses, rather than gross income alone.
Mohd Rahim therefore suggested that the government conduct regular assessments based on income levels, number of dependants, place of residence and spending patterns to ensure that assistance remained sufficient and met the actual needs of recipients.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9, announced that the combined allocation for STR and SARA would increase to RM16 billion from RM15 billion, with all STR recipients eligible for SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year.
The Finance Minister said Malaysians aged 18 and above who were not STR recipients would receive RM100 in SARA MADANI assistance on two occasions, once before Aidilfitri and again in conjunction with the country's 70th National Day.
He said the assistance would benefit up to nine million STR recipients and another 13 million Malaysians, including those in the middle-income (M40) group. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Adly admits Bukit Katil 'a challenge', defends performance amid criticism
Article:
MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan chairman Adly Zahari has acknowledged that retaining the Bukit Katil seat would be challenging due to the cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional.
Adly said the BN-PN cooperation put him at a disadvantage on paper, but he remained confident that his track record and work in the constituency would count in his favour.
He said voters should assess his performance based on the initiatives and development projects delivered during his tenure, rather than political alignments alone.
"I do not deny that, with the existing BN-PN combination, I am in a rather challenging position when it comes to winning.
"But elections are not decided on paper. Ultimately, it depends on the people," he said in a podcast interview with BH Online.
Addressing criticism over his attendance in the constituency due to his responsibilities as Alor Gajah member of parliament and deputy defence minister, Adly said he continued to monitor the initiatives undertaken in Bukit Katil.
He said Bukit Katil had also benefited from development projects channelled through the Defence Ministry's Civil-Military Cooperation (CIMIC) programme.
The programme, he said, involved members of the armed forces using their technical and engineering expertise to carry out community development projects.
He said the projects were planned earlier in the year and were not introduced specifically for the election campaign.
Among the other ongoing and completed initiatives were the construction works to improve schools, public facilities and surau.
"I may have less time, but I have more budget to make up for it.
"If people say I am often not around, they should also remember that I have brought more funding to Bukit Katil compared with other assemblymen," he said.
Adly, however, acknowledged that not all requests from residents had been fulfilled.
Among them was a flooding issue in Balai Panjang involving three to four houses, which would require land acquisition before drainage improvements could be carried out.
"Perhaps in the next term, we can manage the land acquisition and improve the drainage system," he said.
Voters should consider both the initiatives delivered and the outstanding issues when evaluating his performance, said Adly.
He said PH would continue to focus on offering voters the best possible service, adding that the outcome of the election would ultimately depend on public support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Armed syndicates make migrant-smuggling crackdown harder, says MMEA chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Syndicates smuggling illegal immigrants into the country are believed to be arming themselves with pistols and rifles to protect their operations and confront enforcement personnel attempting to foil their activities in Malaysian waters.
This has made efforts by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) to curb the smuggling increasingly challenging, as the syndicates are believed to be prepared to use force to prevent their routes and operations from being disrupted.
The threat posed by the smugglers was highlighted last week when an MMEA personnel was killed and three others injured in a collision during a special operation to intercept a boat suspected of carrying illegal immigrants off Kuala Sungai Padang, Perlis.
MMEA director-general Admiral (Maritime) Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said operations to curb the activities were increasingly challenging, not only because of the syndicates' constantly changing tactics but also the possibility that they possessed firearms to protect their operations and evade enforcement.
He said the syndicates were willing to spend large sums of money on boats fitted with high-powered engines to ensure faster journeys and make it easier to evade detection.
Rosli said the agency had also received information that residents along Sungai Kelantan, particularly between Tumpat and Kuala Besar, had been threatened against leaking information about the syndicates' activities and boat landing locations.
"Based on the information obtained, the fees charged can range from RM5,000 to RM25,000 per person for each illegal immigrant brought into Malaysia, depending on the route, destination and services provided by the syndicate.
"Therefore, the safety of personnel is always given priority during operations, especially when dealing with suspects believed to be involved in smuggling activities," he told Utusan Malaysia yesterday.
Last week, Leading Seaman (Technical)
Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan
, 41, from the Intelligence Unit of the Kedah/Perlis Maritime Headquarters, died after the boat he was in struck a concrete block in Sungai Padang, Perlis, while pursuing suspects.
The collision also threw three other MMEA personnel overboard.
Kedah and Perlis Maritime director First Admiral (Maritime) Romli Mustafa said the personnel had detected a boat fitted with an outboard engine and carrying illegal immigrants about 11pm in waters near Kuala Sanglang.
He said the personnel gave chase before the two boats pressed against each other in the darkness.
Rosli said migrant smuggling syndicates often exploited remote coastal areas, small islands, river mouths and mangrove areas as temporary transit points before bringing the illegal immigrants ashore.
He said these locations frequently changed according to the syndicates' modus operandi and the latest intelligence.
The agency did not focus on any single location but instead adopted an intelligence-led enforcement approach, conducting patrols based on risk assessments and the latest intelligence.
"The MMEA will not compromise in controlling Malaysian waters and will continue to step up sea and air patrols, special operations, intelligence gathering and the use of maritime surveillance systems.
"This is to ensure that any attempt to bring in illegal immigrants can be detected and curbed effectively to safeguard the security and sovereignty of the nation's waters," he said.
He added that Perak, Selangor, Melaka, Johor and Sabah had been identified as among the main landing points for illegal immigrants, based on geographical factors, strategic locations and risk assessments of maritime smuggling routes.
He said these areas had features such as long coastlines, small islands, river mouths, mangrove areas and proximity to international maritime routes, which were often exploited by smuggling syndicates.
"In Sabah, the threat of illegal immigrant landings is more pronounced given its location close to international borders," he said.
Eleven foreigners, including nine undocumented Myanmar migrants and two Thai boat skippers,
are being investigated for murder
under Section 302 of the Penal Code over Roshaimi's death.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JS-SEZ investment pipeline hits RM88.83bil, 12,796 jobs linked to projects
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) has attracted RM88.83 billion in approved investments, with RM40.3 billion already implemented.
It is an early indication of the cross-border economic initiative's ability to translate investment commitments into economic activity.
The investments, approved between January last year and June this year under the purview of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), were associated with 12,796 jobs from projects already implemented.
The overall investment pipeline is expected to generate 28,755 potential employment opportunities, according to a joint statement issued after the inaugural Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) meeting in Singapore yesterday.
The meeting
, co-chaired by Malaysia's Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir and Singapore's Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat, marked a shift towards closer ministerial oversight of the zone's implementation, investment realisation and supporting infrastructure.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi, who attended the meeting, said the establishment of JSCMC marked a new phase in bilateral cooperation, extending beyond the development of Iskandar Malaysia to cover the implementation of JS-SEZ, transportation and the movement of people and goods across the border.
"This meeting marks a new phase in cooperation between Malaysia and Singapore, particularly in strengthening the implementation of the JS-SEZ," he said in a statement today.
He said both countries had agreed to establish working groups to coordinate and monitor agreed initiatives, ensuring that plans were translated into concrete action.
Onn Hafiz said Johor would continue strengthening its infrastructure, facilitating investments and developing local talent to ensure Johoreans were equipped to benefit from employment opportunities generated by the economic zone.
The focus on implementation comes as both governments work towards putting the institutional, regulatory and operational frameworks required to support the JS-SEZ in place.
Among the initiatives highlighted at the meeting were the development of Nexus Sedenak as an industrial and supply chain hub, improved infrastructure and transport connectivity, facilitation of strategic investments and efforts to strengthen financial services in Forest City.
Both governments also took note of Malaysia's initiatives under Budget 2027 to complement the zone's development.
The upcoming JS-SEZ masterplan and investment blueprint is expected to be launched in December, providing a longer-term framework for investment promotion, infrastructure planning and economic integration between Johor and Singapore.
Akmal said both countries had also agreed to organise a joint investment forum in Malaysia by the first quarter of 2027 to sustain investor interest and build on the zone's momentum.
Chee said the committee had made good progress since its establishment, describing the inaugural meeting as productive and fruitful.
He said closer cooperation was needed in talent development, trade and investment facilitation, as well as the movement of people and goods.
Both sides are also looking at improving cross-border connectivity, including taxi services and the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, which is targeted to begin operations in February 2027.
The committee also received updates on investment missions, project implementation, infrastructure and utilities planning, and talent development collaborations.

Title: Melaka election: PH open to supporters backing Bersatu candidates
Article:
MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan has no objection if its supporters vote for Bersatu candidates in constituencies not contested by the coalition in the election.
Its chairman, Adly Zahari, said although there was no formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu, the approach taken in this election was aimed at minimising clashes with the party led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, thereby creating room for such support.
He said PH also hoped Bersatu would adopt a similar approach by supporting PH candidates in constituencies contested by the coalition.
"Basically, we know that our rivals are Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional. So, our supporters would not want to vote for BN or PN.
"As such, in constituencies we are not contesting, there may be an opportunity for our supporters to back Bersatu, which shares similar aspirations.
"At the PH level, we welcome such support," he said in a 16th Melaka election special podcast on BH Online.
In the upcoming election, PH is fielding candidates in 24 state seats, while Bersatu is contesting seven, three of which will see clashes between the two parties.
Adly, who is also Amanah vice-president, said although Bersatu had signed a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) with representatives of the Madani government to ensure political stability, this did not necessarily guarantee political cooperation between them.
He said PH faced challenges in building such cooperation, particularly because of its history of political ties with Bersatu, which continued to influence the acceptance of some grassroots supporters.
"That is the nature of politics; there are always dynamics involved. We also face challenges, as not all our supporters are able to accept this cooperation.
"This is because we have to deal with past issues involving the party (Bersatu).  Building political consensus or cooperation is not easy.
"Old sentiments continue to haunt us, and even the machinery is not working together. We see that every time there is cooperation, it comes with its own challenges," he said.
Asked whether PH and Bersatu would share campaign platforms during the election campaign, Adly, who is also Alor Gajah member of parliament, said both parties were expected to campaign separately for now.
He said establishing cooperation between their grassroots machinery could take longer to materialise.
"What we welcome at this stage is support. There may not be enough time to establish collaboration between our campaign machinery.
"But we welcome support from all quarters for PH. That is all," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar warns Malaysia a cyberattack target, orders top-level briefings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is among the countries considered potential targets of cyberattacks, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said that while not all information could be disclosed, the country's digital capabilities and its stance on certain international issues, particularly Gaza, had placed it in the spotlight.
"Malaysia is certainly among those considered a target," he said.
Anwar was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who asked whether Malaysia was considered a target based on available intelligence and the extent of the threat.
Earlier, Anwar said the government had taken note of moves by several countries, including the European Union, Canada and Japan, to advise their citizens to maintain food stocks.
He cited an uncertain international situation following cyberattacks abroad that had shut down Belgium's national tax portal, compromised the identity records of almost nine million Danes, disrupted the US Federal Election Commission's filing system for 41 hours and exposed the personal records of more than 100,000 Japanese police personnel.
Anwar said the government was also monitoring developments involving the Middle East conflict, Yemen and the Red Sea.
He proposed that National Security Council (NSC) director-general Datuk Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin deliver a special closed-door briefing to all MPs within the next day or two.
"I believe this matter is very important because, based on information obtained yesterday evening and this morning, including from the Home Minister (Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail), we must not take it lightly," he said.
"I seek the cooperation of all members of parliament, from both the government and opposition, to give the NSC space in the next day or two to brief them on the latest developments."
Anwar said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar would chair a meeting with all relevant departments this afternoon, while Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour would hold a special session with financial institutions.
He said a special NSC meeting was held yesterday to study the implications of the developments, focusing on digital and hybrid cyberattacks, possible nuclear fallout from threats against Gulf states, particularly Iran, and the impact of European political developments on administrative systems.
Anwar outlined five measures to address the threats, including strengthening coordination among ministries and agencies, improving preparedness against domestic and external threats, and enhancing protection for strategic infrastructure and sectors.
"This includes energy, transport, finance and food supply," he said.
The other two measures involve improving public and community preparedness, as well as strengthening agencies' capabilities and use of technology to safeguard against cyberattacks.
On public preparedness, Anwar said the NSC had advised him to issue the statement to remind MPs and the public that the threat was not distant.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US signals progress in talks with Iran to avert renewed war
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday signaled progress in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Teheran said "intensive" exchanges were underway while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.
A deal with Teheran "could happen," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, a day before crucial US midterm elections. He added that "Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible."
Vice President JD Vance separately said that both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement.
"We've certainly made some progress. We'll see if we can make some more," Vance told reporters on Monday.
Oil prices, sent rocketing by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor, plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict.
Trump also pointed to tumbling oil prices on his social media post.
The renewed diplomatic signals come ahead of Tuesday's midterms, in which Trump's Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress despite voter dissatisfaction over the war and higher fuel prices.
Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators.
"Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive," Araghchi said in a video interview with the official IRNA news agency.
"Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations."
China also urged a return to negotiations, while Iran's security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.
Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from the US were "an acknowledgement of our victory."
But Trump had previously kept up his threats against Iran, telling a campaign rally that at "some point we're going to have to give them the hammer."
- 'GOOD-FAITH APPROACH' -
A senior Iranian official said Teheran was ready to open Strait of Hormuz, an export conduit for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days – as long as Washington agrees to its list of demands.
In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
Chinese President Xi Jinping also discussed the war with Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday – the first visit to China by the Gulf nation's head of state since diplomatic ties were established.
"The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely," an Omani statement said.
- 'NO COMPROMISES' -
China held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday as well.
Beijing supports Teheran in "safeguarding its own sovereignty and security," Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.
Bagheri told Wang that "Teheran's stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard," state TV reported.
In an interview with Al Jazeera released Sunday, Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.
He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed recently and reduce American troop numbers in the region.
On Saturday, Trump said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Teheran denies is such a facility.
Baqaei warned that any act of aggression against Iran "will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response."--AFP

Title: Rining's dedication keeps Lun Bawang musical tapi tradition alive
Article:
KUCHING: As the clock approaches 10.30pm and the bustle of the city begins to fade, Rining Peter Paris's creative world comes alive.
With a cup of black coffee and reggae music playing softly in the background, the 53-year-old musician retreats to his backyard workshop to craft the
tapi
or
tapik,
a traditional two-stringed instrument of Sarawak's Lun Bawang community.
Originally from the Ba'kelalan highlands, Rining is among the few remaining
tapi
makers in Malaysia, dedicating his late-night hours to preserving an ancestral craft through intricate carvings on pulai wood, locally known as
pelai
.
"I usually work from 10.30 pm until 3 am because my mind is fresher at night. I need intense concentration, especially when drawing and carving patterns on the
tapi
," he told Bernama during a recent visit to his home.
While traditional stringed instruments from Malaysian Borneo are often associated with the
sape
, commonly played by Orang Ulu communities such as the Kenyah, Kayan and Kelabit, the
tapi
holds a distinct place in Lun Bawang heritage.
Traditionally featuring two strings, the
tapi
is smaller than the
sape
, which typically has two to four strings, and differs in its tuning, carvings, and decorative motifs.
Each instrument crafted by Rining features a
menudun
, or helmeted hornbill, motif carved into its head, a signature element of his craftsmanship.
Rining said making a
tapi
involves 10 main stages, from cutting and shaping the wood to intricate carving and smoke treatment.
He sources pelai wood from the hills of Ba'kelalan, where the tree grows abundantly, paying between RM600 and RM800 for 10 pieces, including delivery.
[[nid:1569564]]
"Sometimes the wood cracks during the process, but my philosophy is never to waste it. I use the leftover pieces to make smaller tapi handicrafts as souvenirs," he said.
With ageing craftsmen and health concerns threatening the survival of the tradition, Rining has begun planning for the next generation.
He hopes to train young Lun Bawang proteges and devote himself fully to making the instrument by 2028.
After nearly a decade of dedication, his efforts are gaining recognition beyond the local market.
The
tapi
has attracted interest from a woodworker in Germany, while young musician Belle Sisoski has introduced its traditional sounds to international audiences by incorporating them into electronic dance music (EDM).
"So far, more than 66 tapi instruments have been sold at an average price of RM1,100 each.
This proves that the tapi is not only a priceless cultural treasure but can also provide income for the community," he said.
Rining has also organised workshops in his home village of Ba'kelalan to encourage residents to learn the craft, starting with basic tasks such as cutting and shaping wood before progressing to more intricate work.
"I encourage villagers to take on the initial woodworking stages, while I can help complete the finer details, including the carvings," he said.
He hopes more young people, particularly from the Lun Bawang community, will recognise both the cultural and commercial value of the
tapi
and help ensure the instrument continues to resonate with future generations. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azman pledges to bring federal initiatives to Paya Rumput
Article:
TANGGA BATU: Bridging the gap between federal policies and the everyday needs of residents is central to Datuk Azman Abidin's campaign pitch in Paya Rumput.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate said feedback gathered during his early campaign walkabouts highlighted several pressing local concerns, particularly the rising cost of living, ageing school infrastructure and job opportunities for youths, which he said required closer alignment with national initiatives.
Azman cited federal initiatives, including the National Action Council on Cost of Living (Naccol) and the newly announced Sejati Madani grants, as among the mechanisms that could be leveraged to address these concerns.
He said that while basic infrastructure and flood-related issues were frequently raised, household expenses remained the biggest concern among residents.
"Most of the people I met during my visits spoke extensively about the cost of living, besides raising concerns about infrastructure and floods.
"We know the prime minister and the government are working hard to address this. In Paya Rumput, this is an issue I must give serious attention to," he said.
Education is another key focus of his grassroots platform, particularly the condition of local primary and secondary schools.
"There are facilities that need upgrading, with some ageing and the basic needs of students in several schools still not being met.
"I want to focus on school infrastructure as well as academic support programmes for students' development," he said, adding that his immediate focus would be on primary and secondary schools in the constituency.
On efforts to retain local talent and young people to drive the state's economy, Azman highlighted the recent 2027 Budget announcement designating Melaka as a Centre of Excellence for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), in line with the government's aspirations.
"This is a platform to upskill our workers, encourage them to learn and become certified skilled workers. I want to tap into this agenda for the benefit of Paya Rumput," he said.
Azman also pledged to support the constituency's sizeable number of lower-income small traders and food stall operators by leveraging federal assistance schemes.
"A lot of residents here in the B40 group run small businesses and stalls. Aside from the newly announced Sejati Madani grants, which will help small traders significantly, I want to see how else we can assist them directly," he said.
Azman, who is contesting against Perikatan Nasional-Pas candidate Rafie Ahmad and Bersama's Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar, said he was not taking any of his opponents lightly, but remained focused on engaging directly with voters.
"The response on the ground so far has been very good.
"I want to reach out to as many people as possible in Paya Rumput because that is the only way to genuinely understand the real issues and problems here that need to be addressed," he said.

Title: Mexican investigators raid storage unit rented by Meghan's father Thomas Markle
Article:
TIJUANA: Mexican authorities raided a storage unit rented by Meghan Markle's estranged father as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged child sex abuse material, the state prosecutor's office told AFP on Monday.
Last week, Philippine police said they were investigating a laptop found alongside images of child abuse at a former home of Thomas Markle, whose daughter is married to Britain's Prince Harry.
The 82-year-old, who has denied all claims against him, had lived in Mexico before moving to the Philippines in 2025 and later returning to the United States.
The prosecutor's office of Mexico's Baja California state said Monday it had received an anonymous tip about the existence of child sex abuse material in a storage unit rented by Thomas Markle.
Investigators said the owner of the storage unit reported Markle had stopped paying rent for it in 2024 but his possessions remained secured inside.
Authorities reported finding "magazines from Asia" dating back 20 years, without giving further details, as well as computer equipment that has been taken in for further investigation.
British tabloid The Sun first reported last month that Markle's son, Thomas Markle Jr., had discovered the child abuse images while going through boxes found in his father's former home.
Meghan Markle said in a statement she was "deeply distressed" by accusations her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous "troubling and disturbing" allegations.
After the reports, Meghan said that in 2018 she had seen a letter sent to London's Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection making similar accusations.
"It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said in a statement.
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud.
They made an unexpected return with their children to live in the United Kingdom in August.--AFP

Title: Falling birth rates no barrier to Sunway's paediatric ambitions: HLIB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd continues to expand its paediatric services at Sunway Medical Centre in Bandar Sunway, despite declining birth rates in the Klang Valley.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said the expansion was supported y two factors, namely rising healthcare spending per child, underpinned by higher household incomes, and potential for long-term patient retention.
It noted that the hospital believes demand for higher-quality healthcare could continue to grow despite declining birth rates, as families with fewer children may be willing to spend more on their healthcare needs.
The second factor lies in the long-term patient retention.
HLIB said establishing patient relationships from childhood creates opportunities to retain them as they transition into adulthood and later life, supporting long-term patient lifetime value.
Following HLIB's recent site visit, it noted that Sunway Medical Centre was ranked number one in Newsweek's World's Best Specialised Hospitals 2027 (Paediatrics) mainly attributed to its more comprehensive paediatric capabilities, supported by a dedicated children's tower.
"The hospital's position as a referral centre for complex paediatric cases further underscores its clinical capabilities," it said.
HLIB said Sunway Medical Centre's current paediatric capabilities reflect about three years of substantial investment in specialised human capital, dedicated facilities and subspeciality development.
"These investments create significant barriers to entry, as competing hospitals would require considerable time and capital to replicate the breadth and depth of its paediatric services."
HLIB maintained its "Hold" call on the stock with an unchanged target price of RM2.05.

Title: US midterms could weaken Trump's grip on power as Democrats target Congress
Article:
WASHINGTON: Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous second presidency Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate.
Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.
The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran.
All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.
Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.
The 80-year-old's approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.
In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country's future.
"I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy," she told AFP.
- ECONOMIC DISCONTENT -
Republicans insist that Trump's tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.
But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington's Reflecting Pool.
"This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime," he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a "pathetic closing message."
Some Republican supporters remain confident.
"We're going to win. As a matter of fact, we've probably already won," Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.
But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.
Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.
Decision Desk HQ's final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.
- DISPUTED RESULTS? -
Polls can underestimate one party's support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day.
More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy.
The campaign has attracted more than US$11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.
As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.
Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats – with no evidence – of cheating.
The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.
And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.
Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signaled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats.
"I veto everything," he told a podcast Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's manufacturing sector to support economic growth in Q4: MBSB IB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's manufacturing sector is expected to continue supporting industrial production and overall economic growth in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q4 2026), according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB).
In a note today, MBSB said the positive outlook is supported by the strong new order growth, improving export demand and sustained hiring backed by Malaysia's stronger-than-expected gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.3 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026 and a 53.7 per cent year-on-year expansion in trade in September.
It said Malaysia's S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 51.0 in October 2026 from 49.9 in September, returning to expansionary territory and marking the strongest improvement in manufacturing conditions since April 2026.
"The latest PMI reading signals continued growth in industrial production and overall economic activity in Q4 2026," it said.
The investment bank said stronger demand had encouraged firms to increase purchasing activity and sustain employment growth for a third consecutive month.
It said input cost inflation had accelerated due to higher transportation and raw material costs, partly linked to the West Asia conflict, prompting manufacturers to raise selling prices.
Nevertheless, MBSB IB said that rising input costs, persistent supply-chain disruptions and weaker business sentiment remain key downside risks.
"Ongoing geopolitical tensions in Middle East and elevated transportation costs could continue to exert pressure on manufacturers' margins and contribute to higher producer price inflation moving forward," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SD Guthrie's yield drive could unlock RM482m annual profit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SD Guthrie Bhd's ambition to raise plantation oil yields by one tonne per hectare by 2029 could potentially lift its annual net profit by RM482 million, providing a significant earnings growth opportunity beyond fluctuations in crude palm oil (CPO) prices.
In a note, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said achieving the target could unlock an estimated RM8 billion, or RM1.15 per share, in additional equity value, based on an assumed price-to-earnings multiple of 16.5 times.
The target forms part of the group's broader medium- to long-term strategy to improve shareholder returns, which also includes monetising strategically located plantation land and expanding its midstream and downstream businesses.
CIMB Securities said the strategy, outlined by SD Guthrie president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad in a recent interview with The Edge, could form the basis of the group's forthcoming Value-Up plan.
Under the strategy, SD Guthrie is targeting top-quartile total shareholder returns (TSR) among plantation peers by 2032, compared with its year-to-date 2026 TSR of 4.4 per cent, which placed it in the third quartile at the time of the interview.
CIMB Securities views upstream productivity improvements as the group's strongest potential catalyst for sustainable earnings growth and a valuation re-rating, followed by land monetisation and higher-value downstream expansion.
SD Guthrie aims to increase its combined oil yield from a 2021 baseline of 3.99 tonnes per hectare to about five tonnes per hectare by 2029. However, its yield stood at 4.01 tonnes per hectare in 2025, indicating the scale of improvement needed to achieve the target.
CIMB Securities estimates that achieving the target would require an annual yield growth of 5.6 per cent between financial year 2025 (FY25) and FY29, potentially adding 460,636 tonnes to annual oil production.
However, the firm said the target remained ambitious, particularly given the potential impact of El Niño-related production disruptions in FY27 and FY28.
It added that the full earnings benefits had not been incorporated into its forecasts.
Beyond improving plantation productivity, SD Guthrie is looking to unlock value from its land bank through industrial development, targeting an annual earnings contribution of RM500 million to RM700 million from the segment.
The group expects industrial development to account for 25 per cent of its earnings within five years, with CIMB Securities saying it had identified sufficient land to sustain this ambition for at least another decade.
Less than 10 per cent of SD Guthrie's total land bank has been earmarked for potential industrial development, suggesting scope for further monetisation.
The segment generated RM430 million in profit before interest and tax (PBIT) in FY25, accounting for 12 per cent of group PBIT, before contributing RM689 million, or 32.5 per cent, in the first half of FY26.
SD Guthrie has also demonstrated its ability to monetise strategically located land, with three announced transactions this year covering 1,297-hectares at a weighted average selling price of RM15.41 per square foot.
Applying this benchmark to an illustrative 10,037-hectare monetisation programme could generate gross proceeds of RM16.6 billion, with cumulative gains potentially reaching RM10.4 billion, or RM1.50 per share, over several years, CIMB Securities estimated.
However, the firm said much of this potential value was already reflected in its sum-of-parts (SOP) valuation, which incorporates RM9.6 billion from land monetisation.
It viewed positively the group's strategy of retaining significant minority stakes in industrial development joint ventures (JVs), rather than relying solely on outright land disposals, as this could provide recurring earnings beyond initial disposal gains.
SD Guthrie also intends to gradually shift towards recurring development income, which management expects to eventually account for half of the industrial development segment's profits.
Meanwhile, the group plans to expand its midstream and downstream operations by doubling trading volumes to eight million tonnes, potentially through mergers and acquisitions (M&A), while increasing downstream processing capacity by 600,000 tonnes.
The additional capacity comprises 400,000 tonnes at its new Sei Mangkei refinery in Indonesia and 200,000 tonnes in Europe, bringing total processing capacity to about 4.6 million tonnes.
CIMB Securities said a larger trading platform could improve feedstock sourcing, refinery utilisation and supply chain efficiency, while a greater focus on higher-value business-to-business speciality products could support margin expansion.
However, it cautioned that acquisitions could increase capital and working capital requirements, while higher trading volumes might not necessarily translate into proportionately higher profits.
On the near-term outlook, SD Guthrie expects CPO prices to reach RM5,000 per tonne in 2027, above CIMB Securities' average FY27 forecast of RM4,550 per tonne.
Potential supply disruptions in Indonesia, stronger biodiesel demand and higher Indian consumption could support prices. However, the group expects El Niño-related dry weather to weigh on fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production in FY27 and early FY28.
The impact could be more pronounced in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, while Malaysian estates are expected to be relatively sheltered.
CIMB Securities said the 12- to 16-month lag between adverse weather conditions and crop formation meant weaker production could partly offset the earnings benefits of higher CPO prices.
Rising input costs could also put pressure on margins, with SD Guthrie expecting fertiliser costs to increase by 12 to 20 per cent in FY27, although early procurement had largely insulated its FY26 costs.
Beyond operational challenges, regulatory uncertainty in Indonesia remains another concern for the group, particularly over the status of some of its plantation land and compliance with new agrarian reform requirements.
About 2,800-hectare of SD Guthrie's plantation land could potentially be affected by Indonesia's land enforcement programme. The area represents two per cent of its Indonesian planted area and 0.5 per cent of its total group planted area.
The land is part of Minamas Plantation, which SD Guthrie acquired from the Indonesian government in 2001 but is now classified by the authorities as forest land.
The group is negotiating a resolution, although the potential financial implications have yet to be disclosed.
Separately, CIMB Securities highlighted potential compliance costs arising from new agrarian reform requirements linked to the renewal of cultivation rights (HGU), some of which are due to begin in 2027.
Under its interpretation, plantation operators may need to support smallholder development equivalent to 20 per cent of their plantation holdings, although this may not necessarily involve surrendering existing estate land.
The firm said the key risks were higher compliance costs, difficulties securing suitable land and possible delays in HGU renewals, rather than an immediate reduction of 20 per cent in planted areas.
It maintained its five per cent SOP discount for Indonesian regulatory uncertainty.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" recommendation on SD Guthrie with a target price of RM6.52, saying further upside would depend on the successful execution of the group's longer-term plans.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil rises after report of US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
Article:
BENGALURU: Oil prices rose in early Asian trade on Tuesday after a report that the United States had struck Iran's Qeshm Island, raising concerns about an escalation of the eight-month conflict and prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil supplies.
Brent crude futures rose 48 US cents, or 0.5 per cent, to US$105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 47 US cents, or 0.5 per cent, at US$96.93 a barrel.
Brent crude futures settled US$8.66, or 7.63 per cent, lower at US$104.77 a barrel on Monday.
The United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials. Some of the officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
"The report added a degree of risk premium back into the oil price. Just when markets were starting to price in a more diplomatic path, this reminder of ongoing military activity has flipped the tone," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
Meanwhile, Teheran said on Monday that contacts between Iran and the US to end their war were continuing, after days of Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough.
Trump raised doubts on Monday about whether he would follow through on a threatened resumption of military strikes against Iran and said a deal with Teheran could happen.
The US-Iran conflict, which began in late February, has sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which previously carried about a fifth of global crude oil and natural gas supplies.
The Iran war is a leading cause of high petrol prices that are weighing on voters, and Trump is under pressure to end the conflict.
Brent ended October at its highest in six months on concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government certain authorities for peace talks.
Additionally, the US will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10 and 11 to discuss ending Moscow's war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation.

Title: Bursa Malaysia sees choppy start amid mixed Wall Street cues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index saw choppy trading in the opening minutes, hovering between positive and negative territory before edging higher, in line with the mixed performance on Wall Street overnight.
At 9.18am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 2.97 points to 1,622.48 from yesterday's close of 1,619.51.
The benchmark index opened 1.25 points higher at 1,620.76.
Across the broader market, losers led gainers 291 to 150, while 282 counters were unchanged, 2,000 untraded, and 11 suspended.
Turnover stood at 276.83 million units worth RM178.87 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed mixed as technology-related stocks continued their meltdown, despite crude oil prices easing to below US$105 per barrel on hopes that both the United States (US) and Iran will resume their peace talks.
He said the FBM KLCI closed higher yesterday despite a weak opening, supported by the emergence of bargain hunters, while foreign buying also appeared to be returning, albeit sporadically.
"We expect trading to be muted ahead of the US mid-term election later today. As such, we expect the index to trend between the 1,615-1,625 range today," he told Bernama.
Among the heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose six sen to RM10.04, Public Bank added two sen to RM4.81, and CIMB bagged four sen to RM6.96. Tenaga Nasional eased two sen to RM13.28, while IHH Healthcare fell seven sen to RM7.78.
In active trade, GIIB and Datasonic were half a sen higher at 50.5 sen and 27 sen, respectively, and AirAsia improved 3.5 sen to 48 sen. Nationgate fell nine sen to RM1.97, and Ni Hsin was half a sen lower at 33.5 sen.
Nestle led the top gainers, gaining 42 sen to RM96.54, while Hong Leong Bank rose 20 sen to RM21.38, RHB Bank gained 17 sen to RM7.67, AMMB soared 15 sen to RM6.42, and United Plantations climbed 10 sen to RM29.40.
Among the top losers, MPI decreased 58 sen to RM39.20, Mi Technovation dipped 29 sen to RM6.01, Vitrox Corporation lost 26 sen to RM10.22, Hengyuan Refining slipped 19 sen to RM3.64, and UWC shaved off 16 sen to RM6.93.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index decreased 1.30 points to 12,071.00, while the FBM Top 100 Index added 2.38 points to 11,881.66.
The FBM Mid 70 Index sank 77.63 points to 17,309.95, the FBM Emas Shariah Index was 45.71 points lower at 12,055.82, and the FBM ACE Index gave up 29.57 points to 5,313.42.
Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 1.17 points to 177.60, the Energy Index declined 6.71 points to 830.18, the Financial Services Index widened 137.10 points to 18,706.51, and the Plantation Index expanded 12.78 points to 8,715.02.

Title: Oracle taps investors for US$20bil to finance AI expansion
Article:
NEW YORK: Oracle plans to raise US$20 billion through bond and share sales, regulatory filings showed on Monday, as the software giant taps investors to fund its costly AI and cloud infrastructure build-out.
Shares of the company fell 8.8 per cent to US$119.22, bringing their losses this year to about 39 per cent.
Oracle said it would use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including capital spending, debt repayment, acquisitions, dividends and share buybacks.
The share sale is expected to be priced at US$116 per share, an 11 per cent discount to Friday's close, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Oracle did not immediately respond to the Reuters request for comment.
The fundraising underscores the scale of Oracle's AI investment as it seeks to more than triple revenue by fiscal 2030. The company said last week that capital spending would peak this fiscal year and the next, while pledging to raise no more than US$20 billion in additional financing for AI through fiscal 2030.
Shares rallied about 11 per cent on Wednesday after CFO Hilary Maxson said Oracle also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028.
Oracle had US$125.34 billion in notes payable and other borrowings, as of August 31, compared with fiscal 2026 revenue of US$67.36 billion. It expects revenue to exceed US$225 billion and adjusted earnings to top US$21 per share in fiscal 2030.
Wall Street expects the company's adjusted profit per share for fiscal 2027 to be US$8.14, according to data compiled by LSEG.
The bond offering comprises six tranches maturing between 2029 and 2046, including one floating-rate tranche and five fixed-rate tranches. Interest rates, prices and the number of shares have not been set.
Oracle's existing 6.85 per cent bonds due in 2066 fell more than 1.2 cents on the dollar, according to Tradeweb data.
Investors have focused on Oracle's AI spending because it lacks the revenue scale of cloud rivals Microsoft and Amazon and has significant exposure to OpenAI, the loss-making developer of ChatGPT.
