Title: Singapore's Grab lifts 2026 forecasts on strong ride-hailing, delivery demand
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's Grab lifted its annual forecasts on Tuesday, helped by steady growth in its ride-hailing unit, while demand for its delivery services benefited from promotional offers and expansion into categories beyond groceries.
Grab also reported its first-ever core profit in its financial services unit in the September quarter, as more drivers and merchants on its platform used the company's loans, insurance products and other financial services.
Grab, Southeast Asia's biggest ride-hailing and delivery firm, now expects 2026 revenue between US$4.15 billion and US$4.20 billion, up from the previous forecast range of US$4.10 billion to US$4.15 billion.
"Elevated fuel costs continue to put a lot of pressure on our drivers, and we're also seeing some inflation... pressuring consumers. But despite that, the consumer continues to come to the platform, order more and spend more," Grab CFO Peter Oey told Reuters.
Grab's financial services unit reported its first positive adjusted EBITDA of US$12 million, a turnaround from a loss of US$28 million last year, as adoption of its lending and insurance products increased.
Promotions, GrabMall and expansion into categories such as pharmaceuticals and beauty products helped drive higher usage and larger order sizes.
For drivers, Grab is offering fuel subsidies, insurance benefits and lending programmes that can help them transition to EVs, Oey said.
Those incentives are helping boost the number of active drivers ahead of the crucial holiday travel season, according to the company.
It projected annual EBITDA of US$790 million to US$800 million, versus US$720 million to US$740 million earlier.
Grab's third-quarter revenue rose 27 per cent to US$1.11 billion, beating analysts' estimates of US$1.07 billion, per LSEG-compiled data.
Shares rose 5.0 per cent in extended trading on Monday, having fallen 42 per cent so far this year.

Title: Govt open to RCI on corporate mafia issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has not ruled out setting up a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to address the corporate mafia issue in the country.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government believes it should assess whether there is justification to expand the investigation, including identifying specific areas that require further scrutiny.
He said the government was not opposed to an RCI if there was a clear basis and need for a more comprehensive investigation, supported by solid facts.
"The government will continue to ensure that any allegations with a basis are investigated transparently.
"Appropriate action will also be taken in accordance with the law, regardless of the position or background of any party," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website last night.
He was responding to a question from Khoo Poay Tiong (Pakatan Harapan-Kota Melaka) on the progress of investigations into the corporate mafia issue and the government's readiness to establish an RCI to address it.
Saifuddin said police, through Bukit Aman's Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Team, launched Op Viking following information and intelligence relating to money laundering activities.
"An investigation paper was opened on Oct 14, 2025, under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
"Police also detained several individuals, as well as froze and seized various assets believed to be linked to the activities under investigation," he said.
He said that as at Sept 25, 70 individuals had been called in to have their statements recorded.
Police had also frozen and seized eight properties, 11 vehicles, 417 Central Depository System accounts, 70 share trading accounts involving RM323.59 million and 404 bank accounts containing RM85.62 million, he added.
Yesterday, Muar member of parliament
Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman
questioned the government's failure to disclose the findings of its preliminary investigation into corporate mafia activities, despite the matter having been announced in February.
On Oct 20, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim gave an assurance that the government
would not protect anyone
involved in corporate mafia activities.
It was previously reported that the terms of reference for a special task force investigating alleged corporate mafia activities
would be tabled
at a Cabinet meeting.
Bukit Aman's anti-money laundering team had frozen RM4.3 billion and seized RM1 billion in assets linked to related investigations between late 2022 and September this year.

Title: The German Makkabi sports club where Muslims outnumber Jews
Article:
FRANKFURT, (Germany): When they sweat it out at a big German sports club, Jewish, Muslim and other athletes are also sending a strong signal against rising antisemitism, the head of Makkabi Frankfurt told AFP.
Founded in 1965 and named after the Maccabee rebel Jewish warriors that fought the Seleucid Greek Empire, the club was set up for Jews in and around Frankfurt to have somewhere to play sport safely, before later opening up to all, club president Alon Meyer said.
"It is a Jewish sports club, set up to create a safe space for our Jewish fellow citizens in Frankfurt and the surrounding area, for them to take part in sport without fear," he said.
"But as we've developed, we've come to use sport as a way to create ambassadors for good," he added.
"We have more Muslims than Jews in our club, and that is right and important."
About 90 per cent of Makkabi Frankfurt members — who carry the Jewish Star of David on their jersey — are not Jewish, but all of them may experience antisemitism.
"Anyone wearing the stylised Star of David on their chest is automatically perceived as Jewish and is therefore exposed to the hostility directed at every single Jew, even if they are a devout Muslim," Meyer said.
"The moment they put on the shirt they have to grapple with that and also, to some extent, to engage when it comes to discussions around racism."
- Built by Albert Speer & Partner -
Makkabi moved in June into a new 21-million-euro ($23.5 million) complex designed by Albert Speer & Partner, an architectural practice founded by Albert Speer Jr.
Speer Sr. was the favourite architect of Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler and served as armaments minister during World War II.
"Children cannot be held responsible for their parents if they've thankfully chosen another, completely different path," Meyer said.
"And Albert Speer Jr. has."
The complex contains white and blue buildings bearing the Star of David as well as bulletproof glass and CCTV installed in close coordination with the authorities.
Acts of vandalism and serious incidents are rare, Meyer said, but there was a noticeable uptick after the Oct 7, 2023 attacks carried out by Hamas and Israel's subsequent assault on Gaza.
"Antisemitism is palpable here in Germany, including Frankfurt, and it was very much in evidence," he said.
"But in places where Makkabi is trying to bring about improvement though sport the situation has got better." — AFP

Title: Man charged with murder of 68-year-old Felda settler in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Nov 3 — A 35-year-old man was charged at the Pengerang Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of an elderly settler at Felda Lok Heng Selatan last month.
The accused, Muhammad Iskandar Sentot, nodded to indicate that he understood the charge after it was read out before Magistrate Hidayatul Syuhada Shamsudin.
According to the charge sheet, Muhammad Iskandar allegedly murdered Mohd Ariff Md Yusoff, 68, in front of a house at Block 2, Jalan Bersatu, Felda Lok Heng Selatan, Pengerang, at 7.20pm on October 26.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed.
The court did not grant bail and set January 7 next year for mention pending the submission of chemical, pathology, DNA, psychiatric and post-mortem reports.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Nursyafiq Abd Halim prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
It was previously reported that a man allegedly went on a rampage at the Felda settlement, hacking a settler to death with an axe before fleeing.
The victim was found covered in blood, with slash wounds to his head and both hands.
Police arrested the suspect at an oil palm plantation the following day and seized a motorcycle and an axe believed to have been used in the attack.

Title: Rafizi summoned to Bukit Aman over ‘corporate mafia’ remarks, cancels Melaka campaign event
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said he has been summoned to Bukit Aman today to give a statement over remarks concerning an alleged corporate mafia and a RM9.5 million payment linked to PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
In a Facebook statement yesterday, Rafizi said he had been instructed to appear at 10am for investigations under Sections 500 and 505 of the Penal Code, which concern criminal defamation and statements conducive to public mischief, respectively.
The Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) leader said the investigation stemmed from a police report lodged on October 22 over a speech he delivered in Selayang two days earlier, during which he also discussed the court case involving former Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
“I respect that the investigating officers are carrying out their duties as directed,” he said, adding that he would cancel his campaign event in Melaka and return to Kuala Lumpur to give his statement.
Rafizi alleged that the PKR-led government was using the same legal provisions previously invoked against him to intimidate him whenever he raised allegations concerning the purported corporate mafia and Ramanan.
He compared the latest investigation with previous legal proceedings he faced after raising issues involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), Tabung Haji, Felda and the National Feedlot Corporation (NFC).
Rafizi claimed he had been acquitted in the cases he referred to, although he was previously convicted under the Official Secrets Act in a separate 1MDB-related case.
He also challenged Ramanan to take legal action against him if the minister wished to clear his name over the RM9.5 million bribery allegation, which Ramanan has denied.
Rafizi said he had initiated legal action against Ramanan over the dispute, having previously challenged him to pursue the matter in court.
He maintained that Bersama would continue raising concerns about the alleged corporate mafia despite the legal pressure.
“I believe time will show that we from BERSAMA have fulfilled our responsibility to help the community eradicate corporate mafia while other parties remain silent, even if forced to face such legal pressure,” he said.

Title: Road ban stays on e-scooters, but trial findings will shape upcoming laws, says MOT
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Micromobility vehicles such as e-scooters remain strictly prohibited on all public roads for now, but findings from controlled sandbox trials will shape an upcoming comprehensive regulatory framework, the Transport Ministry told Parliament.
Responding to a Dewan Rakyat query from Kampar MP Chong Zhemin on whether controlled use would eventually be permitted along village routes and residential estates, the ministry acknowledged that micromobility devices offer practical solutions for “first and last mile” transit connections over short distances.
“However, their use must be implemented in a controlled manner, taking into account road conditions, traffic speeds, user safety and the suitability of infrastructure,” the ministry said.
Under the Road Traffic Rules (Prohibition of Use of Certain Micromobility Vehicles) 2021, mopeds, Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs), and Personal Mobility Aids (PMAs) face a blanket ban across public roads nationwide.
The statutory framework nevertheless empowers the Transport Minister to grant targeted exemptions for trial zones, primarily through the Micromobility Sandbox pilot programme.
The sandbox initiative currently operates across seven designated pilot areas, covering municipal jurisdictions under the Shah Alam, Subang Jaya, and Penang city councils and Kuala Lumpur City Hall, alongside university campuses at Universiti Malaya, Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS, and UiTM Perak.
The Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (MIROS) has drawn up operational guidelines for these pilot runs, covering infrastructure design, rider safety, device roadworthiness, and fleet operator responsibilities.
Data gathered from the trials will evaluate how micromobility operates under real-world traffic dynamics to guide future legislation governing vehicle classification, mechanical safety standards, permitted corridors, and enforcement protocols.
“The approach also takes into account international practices and experiences, including those of China, Singapore and Japan, which regulate micromobility by setting vehicle categories, safety specifications, speed limits and usage rules according to the type of route and suitable areas.
“This is important to ensure the national micromobility ecosystem is developed in a phased, safe, controlled and evidence-based manner,” the ministry said.
On the infrastructure front, the ministry stressed that micromobility routes should ideally feature dedicated lanes physically separated from motorized traffic. Where road space is constrained, shared corridors could be considered, provided local councils install adequate traffic-calming features and enforce strict vehicle speed limits. Complementing these trials, urban planning agency PLANMalaysia has circulated route planning guidelines to state governments and local authorities to integrate micromobility paths into wider transit infrastructure.
However, the parliamentary reply provided no definitive timeline for legalising micromobility across housing estates or village roads, leaving speed limits and operational parameters for suburban residential neighbourhoods unaddressed.

Title: Home Ministry: Putrajaya open to RCI on ‘corporate mafia’ claims if solid grounds established
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The federal government has not dismissed the possibility of convening a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into allegations of a “corporate mafia”, but maintains that this requires a demonstrated need and clearly defined terms of reference, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat.
The ministry said this in a written reply to Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong, who pressed the government on the progress of police investigations, whether identified syndicate masterminds would face prosecution, and whether Putrajaya was prepared to establish an RCI to examine regulatory abuse.
“Regarding the proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), the government is of the view that the matter should be considered based on the reasonableness of extending the investigation, including identifying the scope that truly needs to be examined.
“The government does not rule out the need for it if there is a clear basis and necessity for a more comprehensive inquiry, and solid factual details have been identified,” the ministry said.
The controversy centres on allegations that rogue elements within enforcement bodies abused their statutory authority to pressure corporate executives into selling company equity at artificially depressed valuations, enabling third-party syndicates to engineer hostile corporate takeovers.
To investigate the claims, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) initiated Op Viking through Bukit Aman's Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Team, opening formal investigation papers on October 14, 2025, under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
As of September 25, federal investigators had summoned and recorded statements from 70 individuals, while executing extensive asset freezes exceeding RM409 million.
The restrained holdings include 417 Central Depository System (CDS) accounts and 70 share-trading portfolios valued at roughly RM323.59 million, alongside 404 bank accounts holding RM85.62 million, eight real estate properties, and 11 vehicles.
However, the parliamentary reply stopped short of confirming whether any of the questioned individuals would face formal charges, omitting the identities of primary suspects and declining to provide a definitive timeline for concluding the probe.

Title: No new extradition request received for Zakir Naik, Home Ministry confirms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The government previously opted not to extradite preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India and has given no commitment to do so, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat, adding that it has received no new extradition request.
In a reply to Pengkalan Chepa MP Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary, who asked about the latest status of India’s request, the ministry said no fresh application has been received for the time being.
The ministry said India’s formal extradition request for Zakir was received on Jan 19, 2018. The government later received a diplomatic note from India on May 29, 2020, asking Malaysia to reconsider.
“The Government of Malaysia has decided not to extradite Dr Zakir Naik to India. Therefore, no commitment has been given to extradite him,” the ministry said.
The decision was based on Malaysia’s rights under Article 6 of the Extradition Treaty signed with India in 2010, as well as provisions of the Extradition Act 1992, the ministry said.
Marzuk had also asked whether the documents and evidence submitted by India met the requirements of the Extradition Act and the bilateral agreement. The reply did not address that point directly.
Dr Zakir has been evading Indian authorities since 2016, when files were opened against him for allegedly making hate speeches and laundering money after five militants launched an attack at a bakery in Dhaka, Bangladesh that ended with 29 dead.
India’s Ministry of External Affairs in June 2019 said the Indian government had made a formal request to Malaysia for Dr Zakir’s extradition and would continue to pursue the matter with Malaysia, while a court in India had also in June 2019 ordered Dr Zakir to show up there.

Title: Johor’s data centre surge unsettles Iskandar Puteri residents, some consider selling homes
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — Johor’s rapid expansion of data centres has reportedly raised concerns among residents in Iskandar Puteri over noise, environmental conditions and the potential impact of nearby infrastructure on property values.
According to Singapore’s
The Straits Times
, some homeowners are considering selling their properties following the construction of data centres and high-voltage transmission towers near residential neighbourhoods.
Among them is finance manager Lee Shi Qing, 38, who reportedly put her RM1 million terraced house in Eco Botanic up for sale after construction began on a nearby 64-megawatt data centre by TM Nxera, a joint venture involving Telekom Malaysia and Singtel’s Nxera.
“I do have some concerns about living close to high-voltage lines, which is part of why I’m selling,” she told the Singapore newspaper.
Johor-based property consultant Samuel Tan reportedly warned that the presence of transmission towers could discourage potential buyers, even where scientific evidence does not establish a health risk.
The concerns come as Johor recorded 4,222 unsold completed homes and 9,946 unsold serviced apartments in the first half of 2026, the highest figures nationwide, according to the National Property Information Centre.
The state currently has 65 data centre projects at various stages of approval, while its operational IT capacity has reached 1,110MW, making it the Asia-Pacific region’s third-largest data centre market after Tokyo and Singapore, according to figures cited by
The Straits Times
.
Residents in Nusantara Prima and Nusa Bayu have also reportedly complained about construction dust, persistent humming noises and higher temperatures, which they believe are linked to nearby data centre developments.
Nusantara Prima kindergarten operator Mohanambal Rethinam told the newspaper that enrolment had fallen from 50 children in 2025 to 20 this year, with some parents expressing concerns about the surrounding environment.
Another resident, Nooraini Jaafar, 68, reportedly expressed concern that proximity to a data centre could make her terraced home harder to sell, despite its estimated value rising from RM400,000 in 2014 to RM600,000.
However, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia professor Mohd Fadhil Md Din cautioned against assuming that transmission lines posed a health risk to residents living hundreds of metres away.
“Where residences are genuinely 200m to 300m away, the scientific evidence would not support a blanket conclusion that residents are experiencing dangerous EMF exposure or that relocation is required on health grounds alone,” he told
The Straits Times
.

Title: Govt to consider proposed Child Act amendments addressing indefinite detention of young offenders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The government is finalising the draft Children (Amendment) Bill 2026 for submission to the Cabinet for consideration, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M Kulasegaran.
He said the amendments aimed to improve Section 97 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611) following the abolition of mandatory death sentences and life imprisonment in 2023 and seek to establish a more proportionate sentencing approach and eliminate indefinite imprisonment of juvenile offenders without a specified detention period.
Kulasegaran said that under the existing Subsection 97(2) of Act 611, the court must order a child offender to be detained in prison at the pleasure of the King or the State Ruler, as applicable under the relevant laws, without specifying a maximum detention period.
“The Madani Government is committed to improving this legal framework to ensure a clearer and more proportionate sentencing approach that takes into account the principles of justice for children as well as public safety,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 at the committee stage for the Prime Minister’s Department in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
He said a Special Committee to Review and Amend Section 97 of Act 611 had been established to examine proposed improvements to the provision, taking into account the principles of the best interests of the child, rehabilitation and reintegration, as well as international best practices.
Kulasegaran said the findings of the review had led to the Cabinet’s agreement on Sept 30 to four policy decisions concerning the proposed amendments to Section 97 of Act 611.
He said the proposed policy decisions were subsequently presented to the Conference of Rulers on Oct 14 for consideration and deliberation.
Meanwhile, on the proposal to establish a Law Drafting Unit in Parliament, Kulasegaran said the move was progressive and in line with efforts to strengthen the independence and autonomy of the country’s legislative institution.
“This matter merits consideration within the framework of implementing the Parliamentary Services Act 2025, subject to deliberation by the Parliamentary Service Council and the relevant staffing and legal requirements,” he said.
He said the establishment of the unit would enable Parliament to develop its own legislative drafting expertise, particularly to assist Members of Parliament in preparing Private Members’ Bills and proposed amendments to legislation without having to rely entirely on the drafting expertise of the Executive. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Johari-led trade missions generate RM59.5b in potential investments, says Miti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Fourteen official visits and trade and investment missions led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani were carried out through the country’s trade and investment agencies from 2025 to September 2026.
Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said the missions were undertaken through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) and the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE), generating potential investments of RM59.5 billion.
Of the total potential investments, RM14.2 billion have been approved, and the remaining RM45.3 billion are at various stages of negotiation and are being continuously followed up, Miti added.
“On the breakdown of realised investments, a project typically takes between 18 and 24 months to materialise, depending on its scale and complexity and prevailing economic conditions,” Miti said in a written Dewan Rakyat reply yesterday.
It added that MIDA would continue its follow-up efforts, monitoring and facilitation to ensure that identified investment opportunities are translated into actual project implementation.
On the trade front, Miti said official visits to countries including Kenya, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Türkiye, Japan, Italy, France, South Korea, China, Thailand, India and Russia had yielded positive results, generating RM6.77 billion in exports through high-level engagements.
“In addition, Matrade continues to diversify its export promotion efforts into new markets in Central Asia, Africa and Latin America. From January to September 2026, these three regions collectively recorded a 23.06 per cent rise in exports to RM69.84 billion,” Miti said.
It added that markets which recorded double-digit growth included Namibia (up 426.1 per cent), Angola (55.6 per cent), Brazil (41.0 per cent), Tanzania (35.9 per cent), Ethiopia (28.5 per cent) and Kenya (11.6 per cent). — Bernama

Title: Russia strikes kill 26 in Ukraine, dealing fresh blow to peace hopes
Article:
KYIV, Nov 3 — Ukraine said Monday that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile hopes of “progress toward peace” after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations.
Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said.
A rare pause in the fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump to enable a mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ended Sunday after starting on Tuesday, with neither side reporting breaches.
But hours after the truce, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes that killed at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said.
Some of the dead had come to collect aid at a local school.
Footage posted by the Ukrainian emergency services showed the building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble and rescuers working at the site.
“Every Monday, humanitarian aid was distributed to people there,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his daily address.
“The Russians carried out the first strike just as people arrived — several aerial bombs. Then, there was a repeat strike — more aerial bombs, this time targeting the shelter.”
Among those killed were “two rescue workers and four police officers”, acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.
The service named the rescuers as two 44-year-olds: Denys Konovalenko and Oleksy Sushchevsky.
“Every day, they went out to help people, working in dangerous conditions and risking their own lives to save others,” it said in a statement.
Zelensky said that after the Oleshky truce, “there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible”.
“With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings. There must be a response to this.”
Russia fortifies positions
The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, which is grinding through its fifth year after killing hundreds of thousands of people and displacing millions.
A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP on Sunday that Russia refused a Ukrainian offer to extend the truce.
Kyiv’s military also alleged that Moscow had used the pause in fighting to “fortify its positions”.
The Kremlin did not deny the accusations, with its spokesman Dmitry Peskov telling reporters Monday: “This is a completely normal practice in such situations.”
He alleged the Ukrainian army had also used pauses in fighting in the past to regroup.
Moscow saw the Oleshky humanitarian mission as “successful”, Peskov added, praising the “good cooperation between all sides” and singling out the role of its human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.
Lantratova oversaw the ceasefire alongside her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets in one of the most substantial instances of Russian-Ukrainian cooperation since the start of the war.
The mission saw people evacuated to both Ukraine-controlled territory and Moscow-annexed Crimea.
The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.
US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday.
President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.
The talks — to be held November 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said — come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.
Cyberattacks
Both Russia and Ukraine said overnight that their emergency warnings apps were hacked in apparent cyberattacks that came hours after the truce had ended.
Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after false alerts of a radiation threat were sent to millions.
The warning system provides vital information about incoming Russian drones and missiles.
Russia has intensified its attacks this year, firing ballistic missiles and fast jet-powered drones, both of which are hard to intercept.
Moscow said that an app belonging to its emergency situations ministry that also warns of attacks had been hacked, too.
The app is not widely used in Russia, where warnings of Ukrainian drone attacks are not as common and typically sent by text message in border regions. — AFP

Title: GOF arrests 1,733 people, seizes RM82.56m worth of goods in cross-border crime crackdown
Article:
TUMPAT, Nov 3 — The Southeast Brigade of the General Operations Force (GOF) recorded 1,493 cross-border crime cases between Jan 1 and Nov 1, with enforcement operations resulting in 1,733 arrests and seizures worth more than RM82.56 million.
Its commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the achievement demonstrated his personnel’s dedication and efficiency in carrying out enforcement duties aimed at safeguarding national security and sovereignty.
He said GOF had strengthened its intelligence capabilities and heightened personnel awareness of emerging threats, particularly the use of alternative routes and hidden locations by cross-border criminals seeking to evade detection.
“We cannot rely solely on conventional approaches or wait for threats to emerge before taking action. We must stay one step ahead by identifying changes in their patterns and modus operandi,” he told reporters after a handover of duties ceremony from the GOF 9th Battalion to the 7th Battalion for Ops Taring Wawasan Kelantan at the GOF Tactical Post in Pengkalan Kubor here yesterday.
Ahmad Radzi said each battalion must conduct assessments of its operational areas, identify high-risk locations and regularly update intelligence information to ensure operations focusing on prevention and risk assessment were carried out effectively.
On efforts to tackle illegal immigration, he said GOF operations went beyond making arrests to uncovering syndicate networks, those facilitating illegal crossings and individuals shielding the migrants’ movements from detection.
He said tackling the issue required a comprehensive and sustained preventive approach, including identifying high-risk areas, those involved and their modus operandi to curb such activities.
“As of yesterday, a total of 921 undocumented migrants of various nationalities had been detained, comprising 802 in Kelantan, 104 in Pahang and 15 in Terengganu,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh: Smart city solutions, bus hub among plans to ease Bukit Jalil concert traffic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traffic congestion in Bukit Jalil, particularly during concerts and large-scale events, has prompted the government to explore smart city solutions while refining traffic management plans to improve traffic flow in the area.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud had appointed consultants to conduct a Bukit Jalil micro-traffic management study, taking into account various issues raised by residents, including traffic congestion. The study is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
She said the study was important as Bukit Jalil had unique characteristics as an event and concert hub that generated heavy traffic, requiring a specialised traffic management approach compared with other areas.
“We know there is congestion. Every weekend, whenever there is a concert, Bukit Jalil becomes extremely congested. Traffic builds up hours before the concert even begins. I acknowledge the problem,” she said when winding up the debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 at the committee stage for the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Hannah said the traffic management plan for Bukit Jalil was also expected to be completed by February 2027 and would be audited by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to ensure its implementation was effective on the ground and not merely a plan on paper.
As part of efforts to find long-term solutions, she said the Federal Territories Department would hold discussions with the Digital Ministry to explore opportunities to implement smart city solutions to help address congestion in the area.
In addition, Hannah said discussions were also being held with Prasarana Malaysia Bhd (Prasarana) to examine ways to improve public transport access to Bukit Jalil, including the possibility of establishing a bus transit hub in connection with the proposed Mass Rapid Transit 3 (MRT3) project.
On a related development, she said the development of Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil was subject to the provision of infrastructure beforehand or concurrently with the development to ensure that basic facilities could accommodate residents’ needs.
Hannah said four planning approvals had been granted, covering the overall layout development order, Madani Hub comprising a hall, food court and bus station, Residensi Madani homes priced below RM200,000 involving 4,218 units, and Sekolah Madani comprising preschool, primary and secondary schools as well as special education facilities.
“DBKL acts as the approving authority for this development. It will ensure that all development complies with the Kuala Lumpur Local Plan (PTKL) 2040, including population density requirements.
“The proposed development of Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil, with an estimated overall density of 1,048 people per acre, is in line with the affordable housing guidelines and PTKL 2040,” she said.
She said the Kuala Lumpur Mayor was monitoring the development to ensure that the necessary infrastructure was provided in tandem with the progress of the project before further planning approvals were granted for subsequent phases.
On pedestrian facilities, Hannah said DBKL would construct 22 kilometres (km) of pedestrian walkways in parliamentary constituencies across the capital, with an allocation of RM55 million, beginning in January 2027.
She said the project would involve the construction of two-kilometre walkways in each parliamentary constituency and was expected to be completed in the third quarter of next year.
“The construction of covered pedestrian walkways from 2023 to date has involved 29 locations, covering a total distance of 4.35 km. Currently, there are no pedestrian walkway projects under construction,” she said.
She added that DBKL was also planning an additional 20 km of covered pedestrian walkways in the city centre to connect public transport facilities with commercial centres, office complexes and recreational areas, including the Botanical Gardens and Titiwangsa Lake Gardens. — Bernama

Title: Over 8,500 postal ballots distributed for Melaka election, EC reminds voters on secrecy rules
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 3 — The Election Commission (EC) yesterday issued 8,569 postal ballot papers to eligible voters for the 16th Melaka State Election.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said 8,041 of the postal ballot papers were issued to election officials, EC members and officers, police and military personnel, and media practitioners who had applied under Category 1A.
He said another 433 postal ballot papers were issued to Malaysians residing abroad under Category 1B, while 95 were issued under Category 1C to officials from agencies or organisations approved by the EC who were unable to vote on polling day due to official duties.
The postal ballot papers were issued in the presence of representatives of all contesting candidates, he said in a statement yesterday.
Khairul Shahril reminded postal voters to mark their ballot papers and complete the Identity Declaration Form (Form 2) correctly before returning them to their respective constituency returning officers by 5 pm on polling day, Nov 14.
He also reminded voters to keep their votes confidential by not taking photographs of their postal ballot papers or sharing them on social media.
Polling day is set for Nov 14, while early voting will take place on Nov 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: AirBorneo, Bintulu Port handover among key gains from Federal-Sarawak cooperation, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Strong cooperation and a close working relationship between the Federal Government and the Sarawak government have delivered high-impact transport development projects in the state within a short period, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said close cross-party cooperation with his deputy, Datuk Hasbi Habibollah, has allowed several major commitments to be fulfilled for the people of Sarawak.
Key achievements include solid support in realising Sarawak’s own boutique airline, the handover of Bintulu Port Authority to the state government, the introduction of the BAS.MY public transport system in Kuching, the Miri Airport upgrading project, and the construction of a new Road Transport Department (JPJ) complex in Limbang.
“Over the past few years, since we teamed up at the Transport Ministry, Datuk Hasbi and I have worked together closely without any issues, despite coming from different political backgrounds.
“We have always maintained a very good working relationship, and as a result, we have been able to implement and resolve many matters,” he said in a video recording of his speech at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Limbang JPJ branch office on Oct 28, uploaded to his Facebook page yesterday.
Touching on the establishment of Sarawak’s airline, Loke said the goal was achieved in less than three years through strategic cooperation between both sides.
“For Sarawak, we have jointly delivered on several major matters at the Transport Ministry. First, during this term alone, we helped realise the Sarawak government’s aspiration to have its own airline,” he said.
He explained that AirBorneo has commenced operations and taken over MASwings services, with all ATR aircraft now under AirBorneo, alongside plans to operate jet aircraft connecting Sarawak to various regional destinations.
Beyond aviation, Loke said the Federal Government also fulfilled demands under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) by returning port authority powers to the state.
On land transport, Loke said the ministry expanded the public transport network by providing direct funding to Sarawak, which the state had never received previously.
“At the departmental level, we started the BAS.MY service in Kuching, a key initiative by the Transport Ministry given that Sarawak never had a federally funded stage bus system before.
“Starting in Kuching, we hope to expand this service to other areas in the future. As for the JPJ, this is the only new building construction approved for this term, and we will assess needs in other locations after this,” he said.
Meanwhile, addressing connectivity in northern Sarawak, Loke said the expansion and upgrading of Miri Airport has been approved by the Ministry of Finance to cope with passenger overflow and spur economic growth in surrounding areas, including the Limbang Division.
“This project serves as an important gateway to Limbang, and I am confident its capacity can be increased. This will allow for more flights, bringing more visitors here, which is vital to stimulate development across Limbang,” he said. — Bernama

Title: KTMB cargo train locomotive catches fire along Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route, no injuries
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed that a cargo train locomotive caught fire at Kilometer 4.75 along the Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route at about 1.10 pm yesterday.
In a statement, KTMB said locomotive M1004 was hauling cargo train No. 193 from Port of Tanjung Pelepas to Pasir Gudang when the incident occurred.
The train driver immediately stopped the train after noticing the fire as a safety precaution.
“The fire was completely extinguished by the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) at 2.50 pm. No injuries were reported,” the statement said.
KTMB said safety measures were also put in place at the affected area before train movements were allowed to resume.
The locomotive was subsequently taken to the Kempas Baru Depot for technical inspection and damage assessment.
Further inspections will be conducted with Berapit Mobility and the Railway Assets Corporation (RAC) to determine the cause of the fire.
The locomotive is part of KTMB’s Rolling Stock Strategy (RSS), which involves 44 locomotives and 246 cargo wagons under a sale-and-leaseback arrangement to strengthen the country’s freight rail operations.
“Findings from the investigation will be reviewed to determine the necessary preventive and improvement measures. The public is advised against speculation, and further updates will be provided as they become available,” the statement said.
Meanwhile, the Johor JBPM Operations Centre said a Fire Rescue Tender carrying seven personnel from the Tebrau Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call, adding that the fire caused about five per cent damage to the locomotive. — Bernama

Title: MACC arrests Kedah policeman suspected of taking RM15,000 in bribes to protect drug trade
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 3 — The Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) arrested a policeman suspected of soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000 from a drug trafficker two years ago.
A MACC source said yesterday that the suspect is believed to have accepted bribes as an inducement to protect drug trafficking activities and prevent law enforcement action in the state.
According to the source, the suspect in his 30s was detained around 2 pm yesterday when he arrived to give his statement at the Kedah MACC office.
“Initial investigations revealed that the suspect is believed to have committed the acts throughout 2024,” the source said.
The source added that the suspect is believed to have received monthly bribe payments between RM200 and RM2,500 via online bank transfers into his personal account.
Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Ipoh police bust investment scam call centre targeting victims in Germany, five arrested
Article:
IPOH, Nov 3 — Police arrested five Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in an investment scam syndicate during a raid on a house in Anjung Bercham Utama here last Friday.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, all men aged between 26 and 43, were detained at about 6.30 pm after the department received information about the scam.
“Based on initial investigations and conversation scripts found on seized computers, police believe the syndicate ran a call centre operation to carry out non-existent online investment scams.
“The syndicate is believed to have been operating from the premises since September, targeting victims in Germany,” he said in a statement last night.
He said the syndicate used WhatsApp and local internet access to carry out fraudulent activities, using profile pictures of attractive women to contact victims at random.
Mohd Alwi said victims were persuaded to join investment schemes claimed to be based in Germany that promised high returns. The victims were asked to make repeated payments.
He added police seized five computers, 10 mobile phones, and four routers, estimated to be worth about RM25,000.
He said all the suspects have been remanded for four days, starting last Saturday until tomorrow, to facilitate investigations under Section 420 and Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Section 6(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63. — Bernama

Title: Ramanan: More than 500 houses affected by floods in Sungai Buloh, relief centre opened
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 500 houses have been affected by floods following heavy rain in several areas around Sungai Buloh, Selangor, particularly Kampung Melayu Subang, yesterday.
Sungai Buloh MP, Datuk Seri R Ramanan said the affected residents had been evacuated to a temporary relief centre opened at Dewan Siantan in Kampung Melayu Subang.
“The centre will remain operational for as long as necessary to ensure that affected residents receive adequate shelter and assistance,” he posted on Facebook last night.
He said the Sungai Buloh Parliamentary Constituency Service Centre, together with volunteers, was working closely with the authorities and relevant agencies, particularly the Petaling District and Land Office, Shah Alam City Council and the Social Welfare Department.
Monitoring efforts were also being carried out with the Royal Malaysia Police, Fire and Rescue Department, Malaysian Civil Defence Force and Kampung Melayu Subang Village Development and Security Committee to ensure the safety and welfare of affected residents and address their basic needs, he added.
“I also urge all Sungai Buloh residents to remain vigilant about weather conditions, follow the authorities’ instructions and prioritise the safety of themselves and their families, particularly those living in flood-prone areas.
“Public safety is our priority. The Sungai Buloh Parliamentary Constituency Service Centre will continue to monitor the situation and work with all parties to ensure that no affected residents are left without the assistance they need.
“May everything go smoothly and may all residents remain safe,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia has 10,036 patients with organ failure as Health Ministry pushes transplant reforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Some 10,036 patients in Malaysia are living with organ failure as of Oct 15, highlighting the need for comprehensive reforms to the country’s organ donation and transplant system to improve access to life-saving treatment.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the need was increasingly urgent as the deceased-donor rate was 1.33 per million population.
He said the establishment of the National Transplant Council (MTK) was a strategic step towards strengthening governance and driving the national organ donation agenda through a whole-of-government approach, replacing the fragmented efforts of individual agencies.
“Through MTK, we are bringing together ministries and agencies to improve coordination. This includes emergency air transport through Mercy Flight, involving the Fire and Rescue Department and the Defence Ministry, as well as police Outrider escorts to minimise delays.
“We are also studying a proposal to include organ donor registration status on driving licences in collaboration with the Transport Ministry. This would be supported by sustainable funding from the Finance Ministry and clear religious guidance from the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM),” he said in a Facebook post.
Dzulkefly said he had chaired the first MTK meeting yesterday afternoon.
He said the reforms would bring three main benefits, including ensuring that organs were allocated more transparently and fairly based on medical priorities.
They would also give the public greater confidence in organ donation, with all procedures governed by the Human Tissues Act 1974 and relevant religious rulings.
“The integrated logistics network will also ensure that donated organs reach operating theatres as quickly as possible,” he said.
Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry would continue to strengthen public awareness campaigns through the “Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku” initiative to ensure donors’ wishes were respected, including by their family members.
He said respecting donors’ pledges and supporting patients awaiting transplants were a shared responsibility. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Pipeline project recovery, airport smuggling and delayed projects under scrutiny
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Efforts to recover payments made for the Trans-Sabah Gas Pipeline (TSGP) and Multi-Product Pipeline (MPP) projects, as well as tighter security at the country’s borders, are among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official website, during Ministers’ Question Time, Datuk Jonathan Yasin (GRS-Ranau) will ask the Prime Minister about measures to recover payments for the TSGP and MPP projects, which reportedly received 88 per cent of their total payments, amounting to RM8.3 billion, despite being only 13 per cent complete.
Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) will seek an explanation from the Prime Minister on measures to strengthen border security and improve coordination among enforcement agencies following an increase in drug and contraband smuggling, particularly through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and Subang Airport.
During the oral question-and-answer session, Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) will ask the Works Minister about the number and value of delayed or troubled projects, the main causes of delays, action against contractors and the resulting additional costs to the government.
Onn Abu Bakar (PH-Batu Pahat) will ask the Finance Minister about the government’s accountability measures for loss-making government agencies and subsidiaries due to poor governance or underperforming investment decisions, including the responsibilities of board members and senior management.
Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) will ask the Communications Minister about the rationale for removing censorship of PG18-rated films in Malaysia and the relevance of the classification, as well as the future direction of the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (FINAS) following the policy change.
Roy Angau Gingkoi (GPS-Lubok Antu) will seek details from the Communications Minister on the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) technology and expertise in detecting online gambling traffic and identifying and blocking gambling servers or platforms, including through cooperation with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Following the oral question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will continue its Committee Stage debate and ministerial replies on the 2027 Supply Bill involving the Finance Ministry and Foreign Ministry.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the Committee Stage debate on the 2027 Budget runs from Nov 2 to 26. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Fewer queues, simpler payments — what Malaysia’s digital government push means for you
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Fewer trips to government offices, less paperwork and simpler online payments could be on the cards for Malaysians as the government pushes ahead with a five-year plan to bring more public services online.
From applying for financial assistance to verifying identities and paying government fees, the aim is to make everyday transactions faster and easier, without having to navigate multiple systems or repeatedly submit the same information.
The
Rancangan Pendigitalan Sektor Awam
(RPSA) 2026–2030, or Public Sector Digitalisation Plan, launched on September 28, sets out how federal and state governments, statutory bodies and local authorities are expected to make that happen.
Budget 2027 reinforces the push through initiatives including wider use of MyDigital ID, integrated government services and plans for a Sovereign AI Cloud.
Here is what could change for Malaysians, what is already in place and when the improvements might be felt.
Will government services become easier to use?
The RPSA aims to make government services more integrated, reducing the need for people to navigate separate systems or repeatedly submit information to different agencies.
One of its major targets, Mainstreaming GovTech, covers services in areas including healthcare, education, employment, business, transport, public safety and local government.
The plan targets standardised processes across 19 federal service clusters, eight state service clusters and 13 local authority service clusters.
It also aims to increase by 20 per cent over five years the number of services accessible without face-to-face visits, while making 90 per cent of major agency services available through digital channels.
If implemented effectively, the changes could mean fewer trips to government offices, simpler online applications and better coordination between agencies.
What role will MyDigital ID play?
Digital identity is one of the tools the government intends to use to improve access to public services.
The RPSA envisages wider use of MyDigital ID to authenticate users across participating services, potentially reducing the need for separate identity verification across different systems.
In his Budget 2027 speech on October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said MyDigital ID had recorded more than 14 million registered users, with logins across 203 public and private services.
For users, the intended benefit is a more consistent way to verify their identity. How much easier this makes applications and transactions will depend on how widely agencies adopt the system and how well it integrates with their existing platforms.
Will cashless payments become the norm?
The RPSA targets a 20 per cent increase in cashless transactions involving government services over five years.
One part of this effort is the wider integration of iPayment across government counters and systems.
Developed by the Accountant General’s Department of Malaysia (JANM), iPayment is the Federal Government Electronic Collection System.
Officially launched in February 2025, it provides a common electronic payment platform for federal agencies that do not already have their own collection systems.
The public can use available electronic payment channels to pay for services registered on the platform.
The RPSA calls for wider integration of iPayment across government counters and systems as part of its push to increase cashless transactions.
The target is to increase cashless transactions, not to abolish cash payments across the public sector.
Will government websites be easier to navigate?
The RPSA includes plans to establish a public-sector user interface and user experience (UI/UX) standard by 2028.
This is intended to make government websites and applications more user-friendly, with clearer menus, more consistent layouts and simpler navigation.
The plan also promotes paperless processes and services that can be completed without face-to-face contact.
Rather than necessarily creating new applications, the aim is to make existing government platforms easier to use.
How will AI and data sharing help?
The RPSA targets at least 125 new open-data datasets by 2030 and 60 per cent implementation of a government Data Marketplace.
It also aims for at least 80 per cent of agencies to adopt AI in a planned manner, with at least three high-impact AI solutions for each major government sector by 2030.
Better data sharing could reduce the need for people to submit the same information repeatedly to different agencies, while AI could help with routine administrative work and responding to enquiries.
Budget 2027 also reiterated plans for a Sovereign AI Cloud, first announced under Budget 2026, intended to keep Malaysians’ data and the country’s strategic information under Malaysian control.
Unlike a public-facing application, the cloud would provide infrastructure for AI applications and data processing.
What changes are happening behind the scenes?
Not all RPSA programmes will directly affect the public.
Some focus on the skills, systems and infrastructure needed to keep digital services running.
The plan aims to increase the number of highly digitally skilled civil servants and improve digital competency among public-sector digital leaders and ICT officers by 2030.
It also targets high-speed, secure and resilient digital access in at least 90 per cent of populated areas and at all government premises by 2030.
Other measures include expanding the Jendela initiative, extending 5G coverage in strategic areas and developing Points of Presence infrastructure in rural and interior areas.
When will Malaysians see the changes?
The RPSA runs from 2026 to 2030, with its targets requiring implementation by individual ministries, agencies, state governments and local authorities.
Some initiatives, such as iPayment and MyDigital ID, are already in place.
The plan seeks to expand or better integrate these systems alongside programmes involving data sharing, AI and digital infrastructure.
According to the Ministry of Digital, implementation of end-to-end (E2E) digitalisation across government agencies had reached 80 per cent as of 2025.
While the RPSA sets the direction for digital government through 2030, Malaysians are likely to see changes gradually over the five-year period.
What will matter most to ordinary Malaysians?
The most direct potential benefits are likely to be simpler online applications, fewer visits to government offices, more consistent identity verification through MyDigital ID and greater access to cashless payment options.
Better-connected government systems could also mean less paperwork and fewer requests for the same information from different agencies.
