However, these remain intended outcomes of the RPSA, rather than guarantees that every government service will be available in a new form by a particular date.
How much Malaysians benefit will ultimately depend on how effectively the changes are implemented across government agencies.

Title: Orang Asli village near KL still struggles with electricity despite solar projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — As the sun sets over Kampung Orang Asli Sg Relang, a devouring darkness comes with the stretching shadows, swallowing almost all sight and sound.
Here and there, in the ramshackle and spartan homes, the soft glow of solar-powered lamps shines through broken window slats. Sometimes there is the flicker of a television screen, accompanied by the hum of a diesel generator.
Solar lamps are on in the home of Yati Yusof, 25, something she is grateful for. Her family had spent the last two months in darkness, broken only by candles.
“
Kena pakai lilin bila malam. Sebab lampu rosak
(We have to use candles at night. Because the lamps are broken),” she told a technician from SOLS Foundation earlier.The NGO had supplied the village with solar-powered lamps and battery packs funded by Google in July, and Bernama was accompanying its staff on a follow-up visit to check on the equipment.
She did not seem too bothered having to cook dinner by candlelight. Her kids don’t attend school despite the oldest being 12 years old, so they weren’t worried about doing their homework.
Like at least 116 Orang Asli villages, according to government data in 2024, Kampung Sg Relang has mostly gone without electricity throughout the years.
What is unusual about the village, however, is its lack of electricity access despite being easily accessible. Located 500 metres off KL-Karak Highway, the Temuan village is a testament to the difficulties of electrification of rural areas, despite the government’s efforts to fulfil everyone’s basic needs.
A view of Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang during a recent Bernama visit. — Bernama pic
In this case, the issue is not necessarily the distance but the size of the kampung, which has 12 households and about 50 residents total. It is difficult to justify the cost of laying transmission lines to the village. And while off-grid renewable energy systems are likely the villagers’ best bet for electricity, they usually require a different approach from conventional energy projects.
Electrification
Malaysia has committed to providing universal energy access to the population since independence in 1957 as a way to eradicate poverty and enhance economic growth. And for the most part, it has succeeded.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DoSM) reported in 2022 that 99.7 per cent of households had direct access to electricity. The figure, however, did not specify the tiers of the electrification, a system by which to grade electricity access.
The World Bank classifies electricity access into six tiers, ranging from Tier 0 to Tier 5, with Tier 5 representing at least 23 hours of electricity supply a day.
“Tier 0 means having no electricity connection at all, while Tier 5 is what we enjoy in the cities,” said SOLS Foundation Energy Access Director Nur Syaeista Khanum Mohamed Fuad in an interview with Bernama at her office in Sungai Besi.
The foundation had provided the villagers with pico solar panels connected to battery packs, which produce enough electricity to light lamps for a few hours and to charge phones and power banks.
Syaeista estimated that the villagers were currently at Tier 1, with enough power for at least four hours of use.
“Our plan is, of course, to get (the kampung) to (Tier) five, but it is a struggle,” she said.
SOLS Foundation technician Ahmad Fakhrul Azmi installs battery packs at several homes in Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang during a recent Bernama visit. — Bernama pic
She added that access to a stable electrical supply was necessary for the villagers’ well-being, economic and otherwise.
For example, not having access to 24-hour electricity means no refrigerators, a basic necessity in the modern age. In Kampung Sg Relang, no one owns a refrigerator or freezer, which makes  foodkeeping a tricky affair.
Otok Singgah, who is in her 70s, told Bernama her son has to drive to a supermarket 30 minutes away to buy fresh meat every two days.
“
Itu kalau ada duit, kalau takde duit, (makan) pucuk ubi lah
(That is if we have money. If not,  we’ll just eat cassava leaves),” she said.
It’s not that the government and others have not tried to get the village to Tier 2 and above. But it is not easy, as evidenced by relics of past energy projects in the kampung.
Relics
Near the centre of the kampung are relics of renewable energy projects that were installed and then fell into disuse.
Near the village community hall is a hydro-solar microgrid. It is no longer in use, a remnant of a 2012 project by Tonibung, a Sabah-based indigenous-led NGO focusing on providing community-based renewable energy options to rural communities.
Opposite the hybrid energy plant and across the muddy road, solar panels measuring about 4m by 1.7m stand atop of several tall, abandoned metal sheds in the midst of dense foliage. Located by Yati’s house, each unit bears a house number. On the side are printed the names of the Sustainable Energy Development Authority (SEDA) and the contractor Times-Lite Electrical Engineering (TLEE).
Both projects were able to provide Tier 3 energy access, capable of supporting medium-load and productive appliances like a television.
Adrian Banie Lasimbang, founder and executive director of Tonibung, told Bernama the hydro-solar project was operational until 2014 when floods destroyed the microgrid. When asked why it was never repaired, Adrian said the funds were not there.
“The cost to repair the damaged intake is beyond the community’s financial capability,” he said.
As for the off-grid solar energy system, TLEE told Bernama in an email that it did the installation from October to December 2018. The company held Operations and Maintenance Training on March 13, 2019, before handing over the project to Selangor Economic Planning Unit (UPEN), which funded the project, the following month.
Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang resident Rapi Aweh plays with his young child during a recent Bernama visit. — Bernama pic
“Matters relating to the system’s operation, maintenance and status after April 2019 would fall under the purview of the project owner,” wrote Haley Khou Siew Ying from TLEE.
When contacted, UPEN Sectoral Section Deputy Director Rahayu Ali said the unit was considering funding an energy project for the village once its needs had been assessed.
“
Lawatan siasatan bersama-sama pihak yang berkaitan akan dilaksanakan selepas menerima laporan
(A joint investigative visit involving the relevant parties will be conducted upon receipt of the report),” she wrote in an email.
Bernama sent SEDA and the Department of Orang Asli Development (Jakoa) a list of detailed questions but received no answers.
Self-reliance
Villagers told Bernama that the off-grid solar power system lasted only about a year after the handover. None knew or had the training to maintain or fix it.
“
Dia orang bila dah pasang, dia orang tak pergi lagilah. Dia orang cakap pandai-pandai sendirilah. Dia orang cakap macamtu
(Once they had installed it, they never came back. They just told us to manage on our own),” said Otok.
Renewable energy experts who work with Orang Asli communities told Bernama that installing the equipment is rarely the problem. The problem usually comes afterward.
Remnants of several renewable energy projects that were previously installed but have since fallen into disuse are seen during a recent Bernama visit to Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang. — Bernama pic
“A lot of these projects, I can say, it’s poorly planned, or they just, like, doing it to, like, tick the boxes. Like,
macam ada orang
sponsor, and then just, like, go to do it, then put it in, and then leave. So it’s like hit-and-run project, lah,” (Many of these projects, I would say, are poorly planned, or are carried out just to tick the boxes. It is as though someone sponsors the project, they go ahead and install it, then leave. So, it is like a hit-and-run project),”Adrian said via Google Meet.
Experts said maintenance is usually the weakest link with these projects. Orang Asli villages tend to lie in isolated, hard-to-reach areas, and repair services there are very limited. Even Kampung Sg Relang, so close to a major highway, still lacks dependable telecommunications coverage. Calling a maintenance person to fix a faulty system remains a challenge.
Centre for Orang Asli Concerns Coordinator Dr Colin Nicholas told Bernama that the approach needs to change, and that NGOs and other agencies should involve the Orang Asli in these projects from beginning to end.
“But they don’t train the Orang Asli to problem-solve certain small issues and so on,” he said.
Adrian, who is also a former senator, agreed. Due to difficulties accessing and communicating with their village, project leaders need to provide villagers with the training to be operators rather than recipients of the solar programme.  Otherwise, he warned, the problem will keep repeating itself every few years.
“One day of training is not enough. Need to set up village committee, appoint community operator. Training needs to be at least four or five days to cover system management to system maintenance,” he said.
He also acknowledged that some damage and system malfunctions were beyond the community’s means to repair.
Syaeista said foundation volunteers and staff provide orientation and training on how to use their system. She added that maintaining systems was easier when they have Orang Asli trainees on their team.
Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang resident Yati Yusof, 25, uses her smartphone with the help of a solar-powered light during a recent Bernama visit to her home. — Bernama pic
“Because we have one key team member there, like he’s able to tell us like, “Okay, oh,
ada yang rosak
, how do I do this? (Because we have a key team member there who can tell us, ‘Okay, something is broken. How do I fix this?)”
For now, the NGO only has enough funds to send staff for site visits every two or three months to check on the systems, which are under 24-month warranty. Once it expires, the villagers will have to maintain the systems by themselves.
The off-grid solar energy system SOLS Foundation provided for Kampung Sg Relang, which costs thousands of ringgit, is expected to last five years with care.
Better than nothing
Back at the kampung, the SOLS technician soon gave up on trying to repair the battery pack that stores the solar energy collected by the panels. The panels were functioning, but the battery pack was no longer working.
Luckily, he had brought a spare pack with him during this visit. Yati’s wall now sports a new bright yellow battery box. A green light flashes, showing it is ready to be used.
Despite the fix, Yati told Bernama she wished they could get more continuous electricity. Still a little light is better than nothing, she added.
“
Kita pun takut-takut juga
(pergi toilet bila malam).
Takut ularlah. Banyak ular kat sini
(We’re also afraid to go to the toilet at night because we’re scared of snakes. There are a lot of snakes here).” — Bernama

Title: Pakatan files police report against BN’s Rim candidate over alleged use of govt assets in Melaka campaign, evidence to go to EC
Article:
JASIN, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has lodged a police report against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the 16th Melaka state election, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, over allegations that she campaigned using government premises and machinery.
Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Central Leadership Council (MPP) member Siti Aishah Shaik Ismail said the police report against the incumbent for Rim state constituency was filed by a PH representative at the Jasin district police headquarters (IPD) today.
Aishah alleged that Khaidirah committed this act while attending an event where contributions were presented to approximately 30 recipients in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration with photographic evidence and recordings related to the incident have been submitted to the police.
“We have submitted evidence that (Khaidirah) misused the Rim Japerun Complex to host the event a venue that should no longer be used for politically-oriented programmes once the State Legislative Assembly has been dissolved, even though the building previously served as her office when she was the elected representative here.
“We also discovered that the food baskets she distributed bore the label ‘MPJ’ (Jasin Municipal Council), indicating that these were government-funded contributions,” she said during a press conference at the Pakatan Harapan (PH) main operations room for the Rim constituency in Jasin today.
Aishah said they also possess evidence showing several MPJ officials wearing attire that displayed the face of the Jasin Umno vice-chief throughout the contribution distribution event.
She added that all evidence regarding this matter would be submitted to the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow, and urged for an immediate, transparent, and independent investigation, as well as a proper explanation to be provided to the public.
“We do not dispute the people’s right to receive aid, especially with the upcoming Deepavali celebrations. Providing assistance to the public is a responsibility that must be fulfilled regardless of race, religion, or political affiliation.
“However, we view the involvement of a Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate in this programme very seriously, as it raises significant questions regarding the potential use of government machinery, premises, and facilities to grant an unfair advantage to a specific candidate during an ongoing election,” she said.
In this Melaka state election, PH has fielded Esma Eazreen Husin, the Jasin PKR Wanita wing Chief to contest the Rim seat in a one-on-one showdown against Khaidirah.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: Police free two on bail, track more suspects with Indonesia’s help in tanker ketamine case
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — The police are currently tracking down several other individuals believed to be linked to the recent discovery of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine aboard a tanker.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said these individuals have been identified, and efforts to locate them are underway to assist with further investigations.
“We recently arrested two individuals, but their remand period has since expired. They have been released on police bail for the time being.
“Nevertheless, there are several other individuals we are tracking down to assist with the investigation,” he said when met at the NCID case evidence disposal event at Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.
Hussein added that the police would continue to collaborate with Indonesian authorities to obtain further information regarding the case.
Media outlets previously reported that the police had detained two men, both aged 40, to assist in the investigation under Section 34 of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Commenting on the case of a Chinese national detained at Hong Kong International Airport on suspicion of transporting two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang, Hussein noted that the drug syndicate appears to have shifted away from using Malaysian citizens.
Instead, he explained that the police have identified several recurring modi operandi in which Chinese nationals are utilised as drug mules.
According to him, these individuals typically enter Malaysia via Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before traveling to Penang by land.
“They arrive at KLIA, travel to Penang, and then board a separate flight to Hong Kong while carrying the cocaine.”
“So far, there have been three cases; two individuals were successfully arrested in Hong Kong, while another was arrested by us in Penang,” he said.
Hussein said preliminary investigations indicate the operation is likely run by a syndicate, with a mastermind orchestrating the movements of the drug mules.
Authorities also believe the syndicate arranges for new passports for the Chinese nationals involved before they travel to Malaysia.
Commenting on the choice of Penang as a transit point, Hussein suggested that this tactic might be intended to mislead law enforcement by altering flight routes.
Media outlets previously reported that a 25-year-old Chinese national was detained at Hong Kong International Airport on October 22, suspected of carrying two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang with the promised a payment of RMB 2,000 (approximately RM 1,200) to transport the drugs. — Bernama

Title: Investment, love and job scams: Nine locals among 141 arrested as Penang police bust 14 online call centres
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police arrested 141 individuals, including nine locals, in 14 raids on call centres suspected of conducting various online scam operations in the state from October 9 to 29.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the state Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) operation involved five raids in Timur Laut district, six in Barat Daya district, and three in Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT), following intelligence gathering and surveillance.
“In the raids, police arrested 93 Chinese nationals, 29 Vietnamese, four Japanese, three Taiwanese, two Cambodians, one Myanmar national, and nine locals, all aged between 18 and 48.
“They are from different groups or syndicates believed to be involved in investment scams, love scams, impersonation of police officers, and non-existent job offers using various platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok,” he told a press conference at the Penang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
He said the syndicates are believed to have rented houses in recent months to carry out their operations, using Penang as a base to target victims mainly overseas, including in China, Japan, the United States, Brazil and Hong Kong.
Lim said police also seized equipment, including mobile phones, laptops, tablets, internet routers, electronic equipment and computer accessories, believed to be used in the syndicates’ operations, valued at RM1.4 million.
He added police were investigating potential abuse of immigration passes and facilities for illegal activities, although most foreigners detained entered Malaysia legally with valid passports.
All suspects have been remanded, and the case is being investigated under Section 420 read together with Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Section 6(3) and Section 15(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63. — Bernama

Title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash; seek 15 more suspects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in an altercation involving a group of individuals outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night.
Cheras police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause.
“We urge the public not to speculate about the incident as investigations are still ongoing,” he told a press conference at the Cheras district police headquarters here today.
He said police had arrested nine people, including a woman, aged between 16 and 44, to assist in the investigation and seized several items believed to have been used in the incident.
Two of those arrested, aged 32 and 44, were identified as the main suspects.
“All nine were remanded for one to three days, while six had previous criminal and drug-related records,” he said.
Police are also tracking down about 15 others believed to have been involved in the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting with weapons.
Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station’s Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.
The arrests were made near the scene after police received information about a fight involving a group of people at about 11pm. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest man at Penang airport over RM3.2m cannabis bound for London; RM1.05m drugs seized in Jelutong
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Police arrested a local man in possession of 40 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds, valued at RM3.2 million, which were allegedly being smuggled to London. The arrest took place during a raid at Penang International Airport (PIA) in Bayan Lepas on October 18.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the 28-year-old man, who hails from Miri, Sarawak, was apprehended at about 5pm while in the airport’s waiting area and the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage.
“Preliminary investigations revealed that the man, acting as a ‘drug mule,’ claimed he was instructed by an individual to transport the drugs to London. It is believed that this was the suspect’s first time participating in cross-border drug smuggling via air travel.
“The suspect allegedly acted as a courier, receiving a payment of RM9,000 for the trip,” he said during a press conference at the Penang contingent police headquarters here today.
He added that an initial urine screening test indicated that the man who is currently unemployed tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine. A background check further revealed that he has two prior criminal records.
In a separate case, Lim said police arrested three individuals, including a Chinese national woman, during a raid at an apartment in Jelutong here yesterday evening. Various types of drugs with an estimated value of RM1.05 million were seized.
He explained that police first apprehended a 26-year-old local man in front of the apartment’s elevator, discovering a 1.3-gramme (g) packet of ketamine in his possession. Subsequently, they arrested a 40-year-old Chinese national woman on the 10th floor of the apartment, who is believed to be involved in the processing and distribution of drugs.
“A search of one of the rooms in the apartment uncovered seven kilogrammes (kg) of methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder, Erimin-5 pills (35g), ketamine (20g), and 0.015 litre of liquid methamphetamine (‘syabu’). Additionally, authorities seized equipment for repackaging the MDMA, including a digital scale and packaging materials,” he said.
Lim noted that the woman is believed to have been responsible for repackaging the MDMA, which was then sold to customers who would arrive at the apartment to collect the drugs, following the procurement of supplies from a distribution network drugs.
He said another local man, aged 44 believed to have arrived to purchase drugs was also arrested in front of the apartment.
He added that urine screening tests revealed two of the suspects tested positive for ketamine, while another tested positive for cannabis; a check of their past records showed that all three had prior records related to criminal and narcotics offences.
They have all been remanded to assist with the investigation under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Operasi Payung: Education Ministry boosts flood prep for SPM candidates, says deputy D-G
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Nov 2 — The Education Ministry is stepping up preparations for the North-east Monsoon (MTL) to ensure that Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas can sit for their examinations safely and comfortably through Operasi Payung.
Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation was aimed at helping candidates in flood-affected areas sit for their examinations without disruption.
He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations.
“For example, SPM candidates living on islands in Terengganu will be brought to the mainland and accommodated at fully residential schools. This will prevent them from having to cross rough seas during the monsoon season to reach their examination centres.
“It will also provide a safer and more suitable working environment for teachers serving as examination personnel,” he told reporters after the Terafecta Digital Luminaries Awards ceremony organised by the Terengganu State Education Department (JPNT) at Dewan Jubli Perak, Bandar Baru Kuala Nerus here today.
Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.
On schools designated as temporary relief centres (PPS), he said Nadma had allocated more than RM7 million this year to help the ministry improve their facilities.
The allocation covered toilet repairs and school maintenance to ensure the facilities were in good condition to accommodate flood victims.
“Recently, we were also informed that Nadma would provide an additional RM5 million to support the ministry’s post-North-east Monsoon efforts,” he said.
He advised schools, parents and students to remain vigilant and take the necessary safety precautions throughout the monsoon season.
Parents, particularly those living in flood-prone areas, were urged to keep a close watch on their children to prevent accidents.
“Children playing in floodwaters or near drains during floods can put themselves in danger. Parents should therefore pay closer attention to their children’s safety. Health and hygiene must also be prioritised,” he said.
Zainal said the ministry was also ready to deploy its Smart Support Team (SST), comprising counselling teachers, to provide mental health support programmes and activities for primary school pupils.
The Academic Support Team (AST) would also assist students affected by floods, including by providing academic support at temporary relief centres.
“Although the school holidays begin on December 5, these teams can still be deployed to flood relief centres if schools are affected by floods in November, particularly to support examination candidates,” he said.
He expressed hope that preparations and coordination with Nadma, state disaster management committees, the police (PDRM), the Civil Defence Force (APM) and other agencies would proceed smoothly to address any eventuality during the monsoon season.
The 2026 SPM written examinations will be held from November 23 to December 17, while the North-east Monsoon began on October 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027. — Bernama

Title: KL to get 22km of covered walkways under RM55m project starting Jan 2027, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Putrajaya will spend RM55 million to build the covered pedestrian walkways across the capital city, with the start of work scheduled for January 2027, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Parliament this evening.
Under Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) operating expenditure, 22 kilometres of covered walkways will be built across Kuala Lumpur’s parliamentary constituencies, with an allocation of two kilometres per constituency, she said.
Yeoh said the project is expected to be completed by the third quarter of next year.
“While no pedestrian walkways are currently under construction, implementation for next year will begin as early as January 2027,” the minister said when winding up the third stage reading of Budget 2027.
The new rollout follows the success of previous projects from 2023 to date, which span 29 locations totalling 4.35 kilometres.
Yeoh said the walkways are designed to bridge critical urban gaps by connecting residential zones, public facilities, commercial hubs, bus stops, health clinics and places of worship.
DBKL will also construct an additional 20 kilometres of covered pedestrian walkways in the city centre to connect public transport facilities to destinations such as commercial centres, office complexes, and park facilities like the Botanical Garden and Titiwangsa Lake Garden, she added.
The project was first announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when he tabled Budget 2027.
Under this federal budget, DBKL received a dedicated allocation to roll out urban infrastructure enhancements as part of a broader RM400 million package aimed at green spaces, parks, and public facility upgrades.
City-centre traffic congestion has worsened over the years, which public transport analysts blame on car-centric policies and subsidies that keep petrol price artificially cheap.
Yeoh had said that the infrastructure is meant to encourage citizens to walk or use public transit instead of driving.

Title: Demand for ETS, EMUPlus tickets for Deepavali exceeds offered capacity as 100,304 tickets sold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has recorded the sale of 100,304 tickets for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and EMUPlus services for the Deepavali period, covering travel dates from November 5 to November 10.
KTMB group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the high demand reflects a positive public response to the rail services during the festive season.
He noted that the seating capacity offered has increased by 70 per cent compared to the same festive period last year.
He made these remarks following an event with Deputy Minister of National Unity, R. Yuneswaran to distribute 600 Deepavali gift packs to ETS passengers at KL Sentral here today.
KTMB had previously announced an additional 14,384 seats across its ETS and EMUPlus services to meet passenger demand for the festival.
Separately, KTMB has also opened ticket sales for its ETS and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) services for travel between January and February 2027, effective from 12 noon today.
A total of 1.57 million seats are being offered via ETS and ERT services for the first quarter of next year.
According to a press statement, 102,819 tickets have already been sold as of today from the additional capacity made available for that period.
KTMB advises the public to plan their journeys in advance, purchase tickets through official channels, and arrive at the station at least 30 minutes before the scheduled departure time to ensure a smoother and more comfortable travel experience throughout the festive season. — Bernama

Title: Border control agency DG Shuhaily returns to duty after leave
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 2 — The director-general of the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, resumed his duties at the agency today, following reports that he had been on leave last week.
In a post on its official Facebook page, AKPS said Mohd Shuhaily began his duties by chairing the ‘Commander’s Call’ Meeting No. 3/2026.
“The meeting, which brought together all entry point senior officers and commanders of AKPS, focused on ‘2027 Deployment Plan’ (Gerak Atur 2027).
“It specifically addressed strengthening the strategic direction, operational readiness, and the effectiveness of the nation’s border control and protection with a clear focus and streamlined operations as the mission continues,” said AKPS.
The agency remains committed to strengthening operational efficiency, integrity, and security at the nation’s entry points.
In the post, AKPS also included six photographs showing Mohd Shuhaily chairing a meeting attended by the agency’s top leadership.
Those present included AKPS deputy director-general (operations), Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M Nasir; AKPS deputy director-general (policy), Zuraini Othman; and AKPS Commander for Port Klang, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
Previously, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) had decided that Mohd Shuhaily would return to service with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Mohd Shuhaily was appointed as the director-general of AKPS for a two-year term, from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to two charges of causing injury to two police officers at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28. — Bernama
